title: Prakash Bhatt becomes second Indian after Javagal Srinath to be Test match referee
text: Prakash Bhatt during the toss between Bangladesh and West Indies (Image credit: BCB) MUMBAI: Former Saurashtra cricketer Prakash Bhatt on Wednesday made his âTest debutâ in Mirpur, Dhaka, in the first Test between Bangladesh and West Indies as a ICC match referee. Bhatt has thus become only the second Indian after ex-India pacer Javagal Srinath to become a match referee in Tests. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more In April this year, Bhatt had been chosen by the International Cricket Council in a newly created three-member Emerging panel of ICC international match referees. The ICC has an 'Elite panel' which has five match referees (Javagal Srinath, Andy Pycroft, Richie Richardson, Ranjan Madugalle and Jeff Crowe), with three referees from the newly created Emerging panel added to the list. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines The development meant that the ICC would post Bhatt to officiate in plenty of international games, including Test matches. Bhatt has been a BCCI match referee in domestic cricket since the 2007-2008 season. He has been an IPL match referee since 2018. He has been with the ICC since 2024. He is the first Indian to be included in the inaugural ICC Emerging panel of Match Referees. In his international career so far, Bhatt has officiated in 48 T20Is, six ODIs, four Womenâs T20Is and three Womenâs ODIs. He has also officiated in 67 first-class matches and 75 IPL matches so far. The 56-year-old Bhatt officiated in 13 matches in the Under-19 ODI World Cup held in Jan-Feb in Zimbabwe and Namibia. In Oct last year, Bhatt officiated in the Australia versus New Zealand T20I series in New Zealand. Bhatt played 51 first-class matches (3,183 runs at 39.29, seven centuries) and 38 List A matches (1,007 runs at 33.56, six fifties) between 1994-95 and 2004-05. title: 2007 T20 World Cup-winning squad member named Mumbai Indians batting coach as MI announce new coaching staff ahead of IPL 2027
text: Robin Uthappa with the 2007 World Cup trophy (left) and MI batter Rohit Sharma Mumbai Indians on Friday announced their new-looked support staff for IPL 2027, appointing Robin Uthappa as batting coach, Mitchell McClenaghan as bowling coach, T. Dilip as fielding coach and Dhawal Kulkarni as development bowling coach. The four will work alongside head coach Kieron Pollard , who replaced Mahela Jayawardene last week, as Mumbai Indians put together a new coaching group ahead of the next season. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more Uthappa, McClenaghan and Kulkarni have previously represented Mumbai Indians as players. Pollard, meanwhile, has been associated with the franchise for 16 years. Uthappa was part of India's squad that won the inaugural ICC Men's T20 World Cup in 2007. He represented Mumbai Indians in 2008 and brings experience from Indian domestic and franchise cricket. McClenaghan was part of Mumbai Indians' title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. The New Zealand pacer represented the franchise between 2015 and 2020 and will now take charge of the bowling group. Dilip joins Mumbai Indians after working with the India men's team. title: Highest-ever! Afghanistan make historic leap, overtake Sri Lanka, England and West Indies in ODI rankings
text: Afghanistan cricket team (Pic credit: ICC) Afghanistan have reached a historic milestone in international cricket, breaking into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time and moving ahead of former world champions Sri Lanka, England and the West Indies. It marks another significant chapter in the remarkable rise of a side that made its ODI debut only in 2009 and has steadily established itself among the most competitive teams in international cricket. Their latest achievement is particularly significant given the established cricketing nations they have overtaken. Afghanistan had already moved ahead of Bangladesh, England and the West Indies in the rankings and have now gone past Sri Lanka to break into the top six. Their progress gathered momentum during the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, where they produced memorable victories over former champions Pakistan and Sri Lanka. title: 'We need to win both': Gautam Gambhir asks team India to win 'every match' of series
text: Gautam Gambhir India spinner Varun Chakaravarthy said head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked the team to aim for a win in every match, even after sealing the five-match T20I series against New Zealand. With India having won the first three games, the spinner said the team was treating the remaining two matches as a separate series and wanted to win both. India entered the fourth T20I at Eden Park in Auckland after winning all three previous matches, with their batters leading the way. They were looking to extend their winning run and take a 4-0 lead in the series. Speaking ahead of the match, Chakaravarthy said Gambhir had made the team's target clear from the start. âThe first thing GG told us that it's a five-match series and we look to win every match. So that's the goal. And the next two matches we'll be taking it as a two-match series. So we need to win both the matches,â he said. Watch India fans take over Eden Park! Huge excitement ahead of 4th T20I vs New Zealand India's batting had been particularly impressive in the third T20I, when they chased down a target of 199 with 40 balls to spare. Abhishek Sharma led the chase with a 38-ball 113. Chakaravarthy said it would be difficult for the batters to better that performance, but hoped they could produce something similar. âI don't think you can top that, but I hope they can repeat that today. And yeah, they are used to playing in such pitches and such small venues. Yeah, so that played into our advantage for sure,â he said. Chakaravarthy, who is yet to play a match in the series, also spoke about the competition for places in the Indian team. He said players needed to keep working on their game and performing consistently, given the amount of talent available in Indian cricket. title: Ishan Kishan breaks Suryakumar Yadav's record with historic T20I run spree, joins elite 2,000-run club
text: Ishan Kishan (Pic credit: BCCI) NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan continued his remarkable run in T20I cricket, rewriting the Indian record books with an impressive half-century in the fifth and final match against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The left-handed batter surpassed Suryakumar Yadav 's record for most runs by an Indian in a calendar year in T20Is, while also completing 2,000 runs in the format. Kishan brought up the landmark with an aggressive 61 off just 32 balls, featuring five sixes and as many fours. He now has 1,220 runs in 37 matches and innings in 2026, surpassing Suryakumar's previous record of 1,164 runs, which he had accumulated in 2022. Watch Virat Kohli drives, edges but doesn't stop in Auckland | Exclusive visuals Kishan has been in outstanding form throughout the year, averaging 35.88 at a strike rate of 171.58. His tally includes a century and eight half-centuries, underlining his consistency and attacking approach in the shortest format. The 28-year-old also became the seventh Indian to cross 2,000 runs in T20Is, reaching the milestone in his 69th innings. He is the third-fastest Indian to achieve the feat in terms of balls faced, having taken just 1,345 deliveries to get there. Only Abhishek Sharma (1,024 balls) and Suryakumar Yadav (1,164 balls) have reached 2,000 T20I runs quicker in terms of deliveries among Indian batters. Fewest balls to 2000 T20I runs (India) 1024 - Abhishek Sharma 1164 - Suryakumar Yadav 1345 - Ishan Kishan Ishan Kishan overtakes Suryakumar Yadav's record Suryakumar had set the benchmark in 2022 with 1,164 runs in 31 matches at an average of 46.56 and a strike rate of 187.43. Kishan went past that mark with his latest innings, taking his 2026 tally to 1,220 runs. His prolific year has also been fuelled by his contribution to India's title-winning campaign at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, where he scored 317 runs. The wicketkeeper-batter has carried that form into the bilateral assignments, establishing himself as one of India's most productive performers in the format. Kishan's 2,000-run milestone also puts him in an elite group of Indian T20I batters. He has scored 2,016 runs in 69 matches, with 206 fours and 96 sixes. In terms of innings taken to reach 2,000 runs, Virat Kohli and Suryakumar lead the Indian list, having achieved the feat in 56 innings each. KL Rahul reached the landmark in 58 innings, while Abhishek Sharma took 64. Kishan completed it in his 69th innings to occupy fifth place on that list. Kishan, Shreyas Iyer rescue India after early setbacks Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Kishan's record-breaking knock came at a crucial stage after India suffered an early collapse. Asked to bat first after New Zealand won the toss, the visitors struck early, with Adam Milne dismissing Abhishek Sharma in the second over. Kishan, coming in at number three, responded with an attacking approach and joined Shreyas Iyer in rebuilding the innings. The pair added 107 runs for the third wicket in little more than seven overs, giving India the momentum after the early setbacks. Kishan initially took time to settle before shifting gears, while Iyer was aggressive from the outset. The India batter struck four sixes and three fours during his 50 off 23 deliveries, registering another valuable contribution in the middle order. Kishan brought up his half-century off 28 balls with a six off Michael Bracewell. Iyer soon followed, reaching his fifty in 22 deliveries. New Zealand, however, fought back by removing both set batters in quick succession. Blair Tickner dismissed Kishan, who was caught at deep mid-wicket, before Iyer fell to Adam Milne. Naman Dhir added 33 off 23 balls, while Nitish Kumar Reddy contributed 22 off 17 deliveries as India finished with 191/8. India had already secured an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match series heading into the final encounter. Among active Indian batters, Suryakumar remains ahead, with Hardik Pandya (2,288), Abhishek Sharma (2,268) and KL Rahul (2,265) also having crossed the 2,000-run mark. title: IND vs NZ: Arshdeep Singh creates history in 5th T20I, equals Tim Southee's powerplay wickets record
text: Indiaâs left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh (Image: IANS) India pacer Arshdeep Singh continued to add to his impressive T20I record, equalling Tim Southee's milestone for the most wickets in the first six overs of men's T20Is involving Full Member nations. Arshdeep achieved the feat during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The left-arm pacer dismissed opener Finn Allen in the second over of the innings to claim his 65th powerplay wicket in T20I cricket. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Watch Virat Kohli drives, edges but doesn't stop in Auckland | Exclusive visuals With the dismissal, Arshdeep moved level with former New Zealand pacer Southee, who also has 65 wickets in the first six overs. However, the Indian quick reached the milestone in just 99 innings, considerably quicker than Southee, who took 119 innings. Allen was dismissed in the 1.3 over when he tried to pull a short-of-length delivery from Arshdeep. The ball bounced extra, took the top edge off Allen's bat, and flew high to midwicket, where Ishan Kishan completed a fine catch. Allen departed for just two runs off three deliveries, handing India an early breakthrough. title: IND vs NZ 5th T20I: Mitchell Santner surpasses Ish Sodhi to become New Zealand's most-capped player
text: New Zealand's Mitchell Santner (AP) New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner added another milestone to his illustrious international career on Sunday, becoming the most-capped player in the country's men's T20I history. The left-arm spinner achieved the landmark during the fifth and final T20I against India at Seddon Park in Hamilton, making his 143rd appearance in the shortest format. Santner surpassed fellow spinner Ish Sodhi , who previously held the record with 142 appearances for the Black Caps. Having made his T20I debut in 2015, the 34-year-old reached the milestone after more than a decade of representing New Zealand in international cricket. title: IND vs NZ: Shreyas Iyer on verge of breaking Rohit Sharma's unique T20I captaincy record
text: Rohit Sharma, Shreyas Iyer Shreyas Iyer is closing in on a record held by Rohit Sharma and will have a chance to become India's highest run-scorer as T20I captain in a calendar year when the team faces New Zealand in the second match of the five-match series on Saturday (October 24) at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Iyer, who took over as India's T20I captain from Suryakumar Yadav in June, has scored 632 runs in 22 matches as skipper this year. He needs 25 runs in Saturday's match to go past Rohit's tally of 656 runs, which the former India captain scored in 29 T20Is in 2022. Watch Sitanshu Kotak Press Conference: Update on Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav in Playing XI and more Rohit led India to the T20 World Cup title in 2024. However, the record for the most runs by a captain in T20Is in a calendar year belongs to Pakistan's Babar Azam , who scored 939 runs in 29 matches as skipper in 2021. Japan's Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming is second on the list, having scored 860 runs in 20 T20Is as captain in 2024. Iyer batted at No. 4 in India's series opener against New Zealand on Thursday and scored 42 off 28 balls during the chase of 226 runs. India won the match by four wickets. The Punjab Kings captain in the IPL also has a chance to break another record in T20 cricket this year. Iyer has scored 1,130 runs as captain across T20 matches in 2026. He needs 96 runs in Saturday's match to go past Babar's tally of 1,225 runs, which the Pakistan batter scored in 35 matches as captain in 2021. title: India batter scripts history with fastest fifty in T20s, breaks previous record held by Pakistan
text: Prema Rawat of India A bats during game two of the ODI Women's Series between Australia A and India A at Northern Suburbs District Cricket Club on August 15, 2025 in Brisbane, Australia. (File Photo/ Getty Images) India leg-spinner Prema Rawat set a new record in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy, scoring the fastest half-century in women's T20 cricket. Representing Uttarakhand against Hyderabad in the Senior Womenâs T20 Trophy Elite match at the MCA Cricket Stadium in Gahunje, Pune, on Monday, the 24-year-old reached her fifty in just 14 balls. She bettered the previous record of 15 deliveries, held by Pakistan captain Fatima Sana. Prema remained unbeaten on 50 off 14 balls, hitting six fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 357.14. Watch Indiaâs ODI World Cup plans: Rohit, Kohli, Nitish Reddy & Jadeja under the scanner Fatima had set the previous record in May 2026, when she scored a 15-ball fifty against Zimbabwe in Karachi. The Pakistan captain had broken the previous women's T20 International record of 18 balls, jointly held by New Zealand's Sophie Devine, Australia's Phoebe Litchfield and India's Richa Ghosh. Fatima's knock had also equalled the overall women's T20 record previously held by Marie Kelly and Laura Harris. Prema has now brought that mark down to 14 balls. However, Fatima still holds the record for the fastest fifty in a women's T20 International match. Uttarakhand's innings also featured contributions from openers Raghvi Bist, who scored 72 off 50 balls, and Kareena, who made 44 off 34 deliveries. title: âHe still has a lot to proveâ: Waqar Younis makes bold claim on Jasprit Bumrah
text: Jasprit Bumrah (ANI Photo) Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler still has more to establish in the Test format. Despite Bumrah 's impressive record of 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7 and a strike rate of 42.8, Waqar feels the pacer has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers. But when you talk about T20 and one-day cricket, I feel that in terms of impact, Bumrah always delivers in crunch scenarios. And thatâs what matters,â Waqar said on the Shubhankar Mishra podcast. Waqar's assessment comes despite Bumrah's significant achievements in the longest format. The India pacer became the fastest Indian fast bowler to reach 50 Test wickets in 2018, accomplishing the milestone in his 11th match. He went on to claim his 100th Test wicket in his 24th appearance. Bumrah also became only the third Indian bowler to take a Test hat-trick in 2019. The right-arm pacer has also been highly effective in England, taking 51 wickets in 11 Tests. One possible reason behind Waqar's assessment is Bumrah's limited availability in Test cricket compared with Australian quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. title: Azmatullah Omarzai scripts history after walking in at 5/4, smashes T20I world record
text: Afghanistan's Azmatullah Omarzai (PTI Photo) Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and post 221/7 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Walking in with Afghanistan reeling at 5/4, Omarzai launched a counter-attack that completely changed the course of the innings. He hammered 116 off just 50 balls, striking five fours and 12 sixes at an astonishing strike rate of 232. With the effort, Omarzai registered the highest individual score by a batter coming in at No. 6 or lower in T20Is involving Full Member nations. He went past the previous record of 89, scored by former Afghanistan captain Mohammad Nabi against Ireland in 2017. The record-breaking knock also put Omarzai ahead of Sam Billings (87 against West Indies in 2019), Cameron White (85 not out against Sri Lanka in 2010) and David Miller (85 not out against Pakistan in 2021) on the list. Afghanistan's innings had been in complete disarray after Zimbabwe's bowlers reduced them to 5/4. Several top-order batters departed cheaply, while Sediqullah Atal managed just 17 off 21 deliveries before falling in the ninth over. Omarzai found an ideal partner in Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, and the duo launched a remarkable recovery. They added 142 runs off only 59 balls for the sixth wicket, with Ijaz contributing a blistering 52 off 27 deliveries, including five fours and three sixes. The partnership was finally broken when Ijaz fell with the score at 180. Omarzai continued his assault before being dismissed in the 19th over, having already produced one of the finest rescue acts in Afghanistan's T20I history. Captain Rashid Khan provided a spectacular finish, smashing an unbeaten 25 off just six balls, including four sixes. Mujeeb Ur Rahman remained not out on two as Afghanistan closed their innings at 221/7, scoring at 11.05 runs per over. Rashid also achieved a major milestone during the match, becoming the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in T20Is. title: 400 and counting: Why India are ahead of the curve in six-hitting
text: Abhishek Sharma has hit 86 sixes in this calendar year for India. (PTI) NEW DELHI: India hit 289 sixes in 40 T20Is in 2022. Four years later, they have smashed 400 in the same number of matches, a staggering 38.4 per cent increase. And the six-hitting spree is far from over. It has merely been put on hold for eight weeks, with Shreyas Iyer's men set to resume their big-hitting exploits against Sri Lanka in a three-match T20I series in December. On the second ball of the 19th over against New Zealand, Naman Dhir's top-edge sailed over fine leg and landed 15 rows back in the stands. It was India's 400th six in 2026, making them the first team to reach this monumental milestone. Of those, 142 have come against New Zealand, the most India have hit against any opposition in a calendar year. Watch Gautam Gambhir on India's challenges, young players & ODI series India's six-hitting prowess was also one of the reasons behind their 3-2 series win against New Zealand. Indian batters smashed 142 sixes, compared to New Zealand's 61. In pure numbers, that is a difference of 486 runs. A majority of India's six-hitting has come from the designated top three, with Abhishek Sharma leading the way with 86 sixes, followed by Ishan Kishan (60) and Sanju Samson (50). It also tells the story of why India are the only team to have crossed the 100-run mark in the Powerplay twice. India have smashed 145 sixes in the first six overs alone. Across their 40 matches, Indian batters have amassed 2,681 runs in 239 overs, at a blistering strike rate of 189.96 and a staggering run rate of 11.21. These numbers reflect India's dominance in T20I cricket, having won back-to-back T20 World Cup titles. Renowned power-hitting coach Julian Wood believes India's approach to batting is vastly different from that of other teams. "I think India are approaching T20 cricket differently from other nations. They're batting differently and not managing risk in the traditional sense. Instead of managing risk, you have to master the skill, and I think Indian batters are doing that very well," Julian Wood, the power-hitting coach, tells TimesofIndia.com. "India probably have the largest pool of players playing T20 cricket in the world, which means they're adapting to the evolution of the game quicker. The game has evolved massively and will continue to do so, but India are definitely ahead of the curve at the moment," he adds. Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker. Julian Wood | Power-hitting coach While flatter pitches and smaller boundaries are often cited as reasons behind the surge in six-hitting, Wood believes the evolution of batting has left bowlers with very little margin for error. "Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker," he says. Citing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's ability to hit all around the ground, from mid-off to fine leg, Wood explains that bowlers have little margin for error against such aggressive batters. "If you're going to bowl wide to him, you'd probably have to bowl wide and full. But you have to execute that delivery perfectly. The problem for bowlers is that when they miss, the ball doesn't just go for four; it goes for six. That puts them under tremendous pressure. " India's Abhishek Sharma, left, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP/PTI) Wood points to Sooryavanshi's sixes off Jasprit Bumrah and Pat Cummins in the IPL as examples of this changing mindset. "It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six. The mindsets of both batters and bowlers have changed. Batters now think, 'If he misses, I'm going to hit him for six.' "I've worked a lot with Liam Livingstone. When he was at his peak, his mindset was similar. He knew that if the bowler executed his skill perfectly, he might get him out. But if the bowler missed, he would hit him for six. That kind of mindset is very dangerous." Sunrisers Hyderabad batting coach Hariesh Jaikumar echoes Wood's sentiments, attributing the evolution of T20 batting primarily to the improvement in batting standards. I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier. Hariesh Jaikumar | Sunrisers Hyderabad batting coach "You have to give credit to the batters. People say the pitches have become flatter, but even three or four years ago, similar pitches were being prepared," he told this website. "I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier. The game itself has evolved completely," he adds. One of the biggest changes in Indian batting since the defeat to England during the 2022 T20 World Cup has been the emphasis on occupying the crease and the shift away from relying on finishers to provide the big hits towards the end. Today, it is the openers who are dominating the Powerplay. "I think a new breed of cricketer is emerging. Players who were traditionally finishers are now batting higher up the order. Instead of asking them to face just 10 to 15 balls, teams want them to face more deliveries," explains Wood. "When those players move up the order, the batters coming in behind them are also hitters with the mindset to attack from ball one. That's how I see the game evolving. In five years, teams could be full of this type of cricketer. The top eight batters could all be players who just want to smash the ball. We're already beginning to see that," he says. Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast. "The game is phenomenal. T20 cricket will help 50-over cricket, as we've already seen. Sri Lanka, for instance, chased 430 against India and England. It's great for the game. Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast," he says. title: âHe cannot set the momentumâ: Shardul Thakur explains Shreyas Iyer's batting struggles
text: Shreyas Iyer of India (PTI Photo) Shardul Thakur has backed Shreyas Iyer amid questions over the Indian captain's batting returns in the ongoing T20I series against New Zealand, saying the middle-order batter should not be judged on the basis of a handful of performances. India suffered an 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday after failing to chase down New Zealand's target of 260. Iyer contributed 22 off 11 deliveries, but India finished at 172/9. Watch Sairaj Bahutule on Varun Chakravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav & India's defeat | IND vs NZ Speaking during a review of the match on SonyLIV, Thakur explained that Iyer's position in the batting order does not always allow him to dictate the tempo, unlike the top-order batters. The all-rounder pointed out that the No. 4 batter often has to adapt to the situation when he walks in. "Many times, how you bat depends on the match situation, and at the number he bats, he has to react to the situation. He cannot set the momentum. The momentum gets set by the top three batters, but Shreyas Iyer comes at No. 4, and sometimes at No. 5 if the left-hander is sent in as a tactical call," he said. Thakur added that batting in the middle order brings its own challenges, as Iyer has to assess the scoreboard, build his innings and also deliver towards the end. "You have to react based on the situation and the scoreboard. So it's not an easy position to bat, and once you get set, you also need death batting. So, it's a challenge as to how you adapt to the game, set the tempo of your batting, and finish as well. So he has a lot of responsibility," Thakur observed. Iyer has scored 76 runs in the first four matches of the series at an average of 19. He began with a 42 off 28 balls in the opening T20I but managed only single-digit scores in the next two games before making 22 in Auckland. Thakur also highlighted the additional demands of leading the Indian side, saying captaincy can influence a player's decision-making. However, he pointed to Iyer's leadership record in the IPL as evidence of his ability to handle the responsibility. title: Six years, 10 matches, one defeat: Team India's unbeaten run in New Zealand comes to an end
text: BCCI Photo Team India's unbeaten run against New Zealand in T20Is on their home ground ended on Friday after the hosts handed the visitors an 87-run defeat in the fourth match at Eden Park in Auckland. Glenn Phillips and Jacob Duffy played key roles in New Zealand's dominant victory. India had not lost a T20I against New Zealand in New Zealand in 10 consecutive matches between 2020 and 2026. However, Friday's defeat brought that impressive run to an end. Watch India fans take over Eden Park! Huge excitement ahead of 4th T20I vs New Zealand The 87-run loss was also India's second-biggest defeat by runs in T20I cricket. Despite the setback, Shreyas Iyer 's side have already secured the five-match series with a 3-1 lead. New Zealand bring India's unbeaten streak to an end India's 10-match unbeaten run against New Zealand in New Zealand was one of the longest unbeaten streaks between Full Member teams in T20I cricket. The only longer run among the listed records was India's 11-match unbeaten streak against Sri Lanka in India between 2016 and 2023. New Zealand had also enjoyed a nine-match unbeaten run against Bangladesh at home between 2010 and 2022. Pakistan recorded a similar nine-match streak against Zimbabwe in Zimbabwe between 2011 and 2021. After losing the first three matches of the series, New Zealand finally delivered the all-round performance they had been waiting for. Their batters put up a huge total before the bowlers produced an equally impressive show to secure a convincing win. Longest unbeaten streak against an opponent in a country (Full Member sides) Matches Teams Country Period 11 India vs Sri Lanka India 2016-23 10 India vs New Zealand New Zealand 2020-26 9 New Zealand vs Bangladesh New Zealand 2010-22 9 Pakistan vs Zimbabwe Zimbabwe 2011-21 India's 10-match unbeaten streak against New Zealand in New Zealand ended on October 30, 2026. Phillips, Bracewell lead New Zealand's batting charge New Zealand made full use of the opportunity after India elected to bowl first. The hosts smashed 259/7 in 20 overs, registering their highest-ever T20I total. Phillips led the attack with a brilliant 107 off 49 balls, including six fours and 10 sixes. It was his third century in T20I cricket. Bracewell provided excellent support with a quick 65 off just 25 balls. The pair added 115 runs for the fifth wicket in only 41 deliveries, completely changing the course of the innings. Finn Allen also played an attacking knock of 31 off 17 balls, while Daryl Mitchell scored 24 off just nine deliveries. After Mayank Yadav dismissed Tim Seifert and Mitchell, Phillips joined Allen to add 59 runs for the third wicket and steady the innings. The real damage, however, came when Phillips and Bracewell joined forces. Both batters attacked the Indian bowlers and scored runs at a remarkable pace. Phillips went after Nitish Kumar Reddy in the 16th over, smashing four consecutive sixes. India conceded 32 runs in that over. Bracewell also took on Axar Patel, hitting three fours and a six in one over. He reached his half-century in just 18 balls. Phillips completed his century in 46 balls with a six off Arshdeep Singh. He scored his second half-century in just 15 deliveries, showing how quickly he accelerated. New Zealand collected 85 runs in the final five overs to finish at 259/7. It was their highest-ever T20I total and the highest score by any team against India in the format. Mayank was India's leading wicket-taker with 3/48. Arshdeep, Prince Yadav and Nitish Kumar Reddy claimed one wicket each. Arshdeep also reached a major milestone, becoming the first Indian bowler to take 150 wickets in T20Is. Duffy leads New Zealand's attack as India collapse India needed a strong start to chase down the massive target, but Duffy struck twice in the very first over. The New Zealand pacer dismissed Sanju Samson for four before sending Ishan Kishan back for a duck. The early wickets put India under immediate pressure. The visitors struggled to recover from the setback. Abhishek Sharma scored 27 off 15 balls, while captain Shreyas Iyer contributed 22 off 11 deliveries. The two added 46 runs for the third wicket, but Matthew Fisher ended their partnership by dismissing Abhishek, who hit the ball straight to Mitchell Santner in the covers. Iyer also failed to stay for long as Adam Milne bowled him with a delivery clocked at 143 kmph. title: IND vs NZ: 118/0 in 36 balls! India script jaw-dropping record in 3rd T20I win over New Zealand

title: Time for a shake-up? The selection calls facing Gambhir after India's Auckland defeat
text: Gautam Gambhir has so far backed the players he believes can deliver for India in T20Is. But the 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I at Auckland could force the head coach into tactical changes for the fifth and final match against New Zealand at Hamilton on Sunday. India have already taken an unassailable 3-1 lead, but the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cup champions will not want to end the series with back-to-back defeats after winning the first three matches. Watch India fans take over Eden Park! Huge excitement ahead of 4th T20I vs New Zealand One player under pressure is Sanju Samson . The opener, one of India's heroes from the 2026 T20 World Cup triumph, continues to enjoy strong backing from the team management, but his returns in this series have been mixed: 67, 14, 18 and 4. There is also a growing clamour for return of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who made 4 and 45 off 19 balls in his two appearances in the series. His entertaining 133-run opening stand with Abhishek Sharma helped India chase 199 in the third T20I with six wickets in hand. A short break may help Samson reset and return stronger, as he has done several times in his career. Another major concern is the form of captain Shreyas Iyer . India have beaten West Indies and New Zealand in recent T20I series under him, but his own returns have been modest. After scoring his maiden T20I hundred against West Indies, Iyer has made 40, 1, 16, 22, 42, 7, 5 and 22 in his next eight innings. Before the criticism grows louder, Iyer needs a substantial score to justify his elevation to India's T20I captaincy after three years away from the format at international level. India's allrounders Naman Dhir and Nitish Kumar Reddy have contributed with late-order hitting, but their bowling remains a concern. Nitish was taken for 32 runs in one over by a rampaging Glenn Phillips in the fourth T20I. India's biggest bowling worry, however, is Axar Patel's decline as a run-controlling wicket-taking option. In four matches this series, Axar has taken three wickets at an average of 52.66 and an economy rate of 10.53. Bhuvneshwar Kumar's much-celebrated return has also been underwhelming. The veteran seamer has taken just one wicket in three matches while conceding 139 runs at an economy rate of 11.58. He is the only Indian bowler with an economy rate under 10 in this series, going at 9.31. India need to find a way to bring in either Kuldeep Yadav or Varun Chakravarthy, both of whom are yet to play in the series. Kuldeep's left-arm wrist-spin or Varun's mystery spin could strengthen the attack, but India may be reluctant to leave out Dhir given his finishing ability. New Zealand's biggest threat remains Glenn Phillips, who has dominated the series. In four matches, he has scored 276 runs at an average of 92.00 and a strike rate of 189.04, with two fifties and a hundred. His 107 off 49 balls in the fourth T20I powered New Zealand to 259 for four, and he will be eager to finish the T20I series with another major contribution. It may be a dead rubber, but New Zealand will be determined to win the final round before both teams move into the five-match ODI series, beginning Nov 4 at Auckland. title: India series drive record Cricket Australia revenue, two-day Ashes Tests burn A$20m hole in  finances
text: Rohit Sharma, left, and Virat Kohli return to the pavilion after winning the third ODI match of a series against Australia, at the Sydney Cricket Ground, in Sydney, Australia. (PTI File Photo) Cricket Australia's (CA) record revenue of A$601.1 million ($423 million) in the 2025-26 financial year was driven by media rights deals for the Ashes and the limited-overs series against India. The governing body also reported a net surplus of A$81.8 million ($57 million), but two Ashes Tests that ended inside two days last summer cost it an estimated A$20 million in revenue. The financial impact comes as CA prepares for two consecutive years of projected losses, with deficits expected in 2026-27 and 2027-28. Watch Mumbai Indiansâ new coach Luke Williams on Harmanpreet Kaur, WPL auction and plans for 2027 On Wednesday, Cricket Australia said its financial results for 2025-26 reflected strong commercial performance, record audiences and the success of the international season. In the previous financial year, 2024-25, it had recorded a net loss of A$11.3 million ($7.95 million). CA said the men's home Ashes series against England and the white-ball series against India generated record media, commercial and match-day revenue. However, it expects revenue to fall over the next two financial years due to a âcyclical decline in media rights and match revenues in line with the international touring schedule.â The financial outlook does not include the anticipated sale of stakes in some Big Bash League (BBL) franchises. Australia's teams also enjoyed success on the field during the year. The men's side retained the Ashes with a 4-1 series win at home, while the women's team won its seventh ICC T20 World Cup title after beating England in the final at Lord's. During October and November last year, Australia won the ODI series against India 2-1, while India claimed the T20I series by the same margin. The Ashes also drew record crowds, with 859,580 spectators attending matches over 18 days, at an average of 47,754 per day. title: 'Best player Iâve ever played with': Aaron Finch reveals what sets Steve Smith apart from David Warner and other batters
text: Steve Smith and Aaron Finch (Image: AFP) Former Australia white-ball captain Aaron Finch believes Steve Smith stands in a league of his own, describing the star batter as the best player he has shared a dressing room with. From being a leg-spinner batting at No. 8 to becoming one of the most accomplished batters of his generation, Smithâs remarkable rise has been driven by a rare combination of natural talent, relentless hard work and an unwavering belief in his own methods, according to Finch. Smith, who was once viewed as a potential successor to legendary leg-spinner Shane Warne, has gone on to establish himself as one of Australia's greatest modern-day batters. He has occupied the No. 1 spot in the ICC Test batting rankings and captained Australia across formats, transforming his game through years of refinement and an unconventional approach that has often set him apart from his contemporaries. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more Speaking on Cricinfo's show, Finch reflected on Smith's evolution, his distinctive batting technique and the mental strength that has helped him thrive at the highest level. âHe turned into this absolute gun of a batterâ Finch recalled how Smith initially entered Australian cricket as a bowling all-rounder, with his batting playing a secondary role. However, a significant change in his approach eventually unlocked his potential and turned him into one of the most formidable run-scorers in world cricket. âSteve Smith went from being touted as Shane Warneâs replacement, starting at eight in the batting order, bowling a few overs of leg spin, getting the odd runs as the finisher. Then something changed overnight. He turned into this absolute gun of a batter that took the world by storm,â Finch said. âHe was always a handsy player with big movements, moving his feet a lot. Then he simplified that and everything clicked,â Finch added. Smith's ability to establish himself in the middle order and subsequently make the No. 4 position his own further demonstrated his adaptability. For Finch, however, the defining feature of Smith's batting has been his willingness to trust his instincts, regardless of how unconventional his methods might appear. âThe ability to go from number six and five for so long and then slip into number four in the batting order was extraordinary. Heâs the best player Iâve ever played with by a mile. He says, Iâm doing it this way; I donât care what it looks like to the outside world. This is what will make me most successful,â Finch said. âThat is a superpower. To see what he does when others canât, you canât explain why players like me or David Warner couldnât do it, but he could. Itâs a natural gift, but also hard work, the hours heâs put in. Itâs extraordinary.â How stepping away from captaincy helped Smith Smith's career also endured a major setback following Australia's ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town in 2018. The incident resulted in a 12-month ban from international and domestic cricket under Cricket Australia's sanctions, alongside a two-year prohibition on holding a leadership position. He eventually returned to the international setup and later became vice-captain to current Test skipper Pat Cummins. Finch believes the absence of captaincy responsibilities after the scandal may have helped Smith rediscover his focus as a batter. According to Finch, the demands of leadership had often required Smith to divide his attention between his own preparation and the needs of the wider team. Being relieved of those responsibilities allowed him to concentrate more fully on his individual game. âAfter the 2018 incident, coming back into the international setup, Steve Smith was more relaxed as a player because he didnât have the captaincy for obvious reasons. As captain, so much of your time goes into things away from your own game,â Finch said. He explained that Smith's meticulous preparation could also become mentally demanding when combined with the responsibility of managing a team. âAnd then getting the amount of work he wanted done put extra pressure on him mentally, because you need to get this much work done to feel ready to go, but youâve still got to worry about everybody else,â he added. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Finch also admitted that captaining Australia with Smith in the team initially proved challenging for him. Having previously played under Smith, he held the batter's tactical judgement in high regard and sometimes found himself questioning his own decisions. âI found it really difficult to captain with him in the side at the start, because Iâd played under him for quite a bit of time and tactically, I thought he was an outstanding captain. So, I found myself at times being like, is this the right move? What would Smith think?â However, Smith eventually encouraged Finch to trust his own judgement rather than seek constant reassurance. âAnd then one day he just said, why do you keep asking me? title: Jadavpur University Debars Staffer Amid Sexual Harassment Probe
text: JU Kolkata: Jadavpur University debarred the accused maths dept staffer from entering the campus on Monday till the probe is over. A first-year arts faculty student has alleged that a university staffer sexually harassed her on the sixth floor of Technology Bhavan around 3.20 pm on Friday. title: 'Small moments cost us': Mitchell Santner rues missed opportunities after New Zealand's 3-2 series defeat against India
text: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner (Image: IANS) New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes his side let a potential series victory slip away after failing to capitalise on crucial moments in the opening matches against India. Despite finishing the five-match T20I series with back-to-back victories, the Black Caps fell short 2-3 at home, with Santner admitting that a few missed opportunities could have changed the outcome. New Zealand bounced back strongly after losing two of the first three encounters, winning the final two matches to finish the series on a positive note. Their campaign included a commanding seven-wicket victory in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday, where Tim Seifert scored 93 and Glenn Phillips remained unbeaten on 65. Watch Virat Kohli drives, edges but doesn't stop in Auckland | Exclusive visuals Reflecting on the series after the final match, Santner felt the contests were much closer than the final scoreline suggested and rued his team's inability to close out the early games. "Yeah, I think we'll reflect on that, and we know that it was a very tight series against a very good team. But yeah, I think those small moments, as you said in the first couple of games where, you know, we probably could have won those games or should have. So the series could have looked a lot different," Santner said. Santner highlights positives despite series defeat New Zealand pushed India hard in the opening two matches. The hosts challenged the visitors to chase a record 226 in the first T20I before coming close to defending 180 in the second encounter. Although India managed to win both contests, Santner was pleased with his team's overall performance, particularly the improvement in batting and bowling as the series progressed. "But in terms of a cricketing point of view, there's a lot of good stuff. The batting was really good, and then the bowling - guys adapted brilliantly last couple of games. So, you know, there's a lot of positives. Obviously the scoreline shows 3-2 to India, but could have been the other way around," he added. New Zealand skipper praises bowling adjustments in final T20I Santner also praised his bowlers for adapting to the conditions in Hamilton, where New Zealand restricted India to 191/8 despite a strong partnership between Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer. Adam Milne led the bowling attack with figures of 4/19, while Blair Tickner and Nathan Smith picked up two wickets each. Santner felt the bowlers executed their plans well by mixing up their lengths and variations, particularly after India's middle-order batters began attacking. "Yeah, I thought we mixed it up really nicely. I think that was a little bit with the new ball, and then Shreyas and Kishan put their foot on the gas and we, the seamers, kind of mixed it up. "Yorkers, wide, a little bit straight with length. So it was, yeah, it was good learning, obviously for us. You know, I guess next time we play at this time of the year is probably the World Cup in a couple of years. So you're learning from these games this time of the year," he said. Santner heaps praise on Glenn Phillips after consistent T20I series Santner reserved special praise for Glenn Phillips, who emerged as one of New Zealand's standout performers throughout the series. The right-handed batter finished with 341 runs, including a century and multiple half-centuries, playing a crucial role in keeping the hosts competitive. title: 'That's why I praised my team': Daren Sammy backs West Indies' 2-2 draw, says India remains a 'dangerous team'
text: Daren Sammy Explains India's T20I Challenge (Agency Images) West Indies head coach Daren Sammy has reiterated his praise for his team's 2-2 T20I series draw against India, pointing to the challenge of competing against the reigning two-time T20 world champions after India's record-breaking batting display against New Zealand. Sammy highlighted the impact of smaller boundaries, batting-friendly pitches and the challenges posed by a wet ball for bowlers as he underlined why India remain such a formidable opponent in the shortest format. India produced a breathtaking performance in the third T20I against New Zealand, chasing down a target of 199 in just 13.2 overs to secure a six-wicket victory and take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. Reacting to India's dominant display, Sammy took to X to reinforce his earlier assessment of the West Indies' performance against India. "Wowâ¦. Thatâs why I praised my team for what they accomplished in India. India is a dangerous team. "1. Smaller boundaries "2. Batting paradise pitches "3. Wet ball for bowlers," Sammy wrote. 'We probably didn't have a chance': Sammy on West Indies' series draw West Indies managed to hold India to a 2-2 draw in their recent five-match T20I series, with the final match in Bengaluru abandoned due to rain. Sammy had described the result as a significant achievement for his side, which competed against the defending champions on their home turf. "It's a true reflection of how all the teams have played, especially for our guys," Sammy had said after the washed-out fifth T20I. "We understand what success means to us; we don't ever take for granted where we are as a team and the challenges that we face. "We played against the defending champions, and we've matched them (and) in certain areas we've outplayed them, especially in their backyard." title: 'Everyone has shown the competence to beat everyone else': Gary Stead warns New Zealand against taking home advantage for granted
text: Shreyas Iyer, Mitchell Santner BENGALURU: Home advantage is losing its sheen in international cricket, with teams increasingly equipped to beat opponents in the latter's own backyard. Former head coach Gary Stead believes hosts New Zealand may not enjoy the edge they once did when India begin their tour with the T20 series beginning on Thursday, with the visitorsâ improved pace attack and the ability to adapt to challenging conditions making them a formidable opponent. The 54-year-old, who oversaw a successful phase in New Zealand cricket, including their World Test Championship triumph, said the days of exploiting an opponentâs perceived weakness were fading. Watch Shreyas Iyer press conference: On Sanju Samson v Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and more âEarlier, you played India and thought, âOh, weâll do a green track because they donât have good seamers.â Now they have quality seamers as well,â Stead said. Referring to New Zealandâs 3-0 triumph in the 2024 Test series in India, he added: âThe same way, when we came in 2024, we had quality spinners too. The whole idea of home advantage has disappeared a little bit around the world. Everyone has shown the competence to beat everyone else at any given time. So youâve got to be on your game and be sharp.â Stead, currently head coach of Andhraâs Ranji Trophy team, believes Indiaâs ability to adapt to New Zealandâs bouncy surfaces will be crucial to their chances. âThe Indians are going to have to adapt to bouncy wickets, some of the bounciest possibly in the world. The wickets will have bounce and carry. If the Indian players can nullify New Zealandâs bowlers, then I think itâll be a cracking series,â he said. The Test matches, in particular, could pose the toughest challenge. Stead pointed to Hagley Oval in Christchurch and Basin Reserve Wellington as venues traditionally known for their extra bounce. âIt's very important for New Zealand. India are obviously an amazing Test side, and then we go to Australia and play, so there are six huge Tests coming up for New Zealand. But if you want to be judged against the best, youâve got to compete against the best as well,â he said. With Australia and South Africa also producing compelling Test cricket recently, Stead believes the influence of T20 cricket is increasingly visible in the longest format. Stead also called on the International Cricket Council (ICC) to explore more multi-format series, arguing that longer tours could help sustain interest across formats. âPersonally, I think the ICC should consider playing more multi-format series. title: Abhishek Sharma's 35-ball century powers India to series-clinching win over New Zealand
text: India's Abhishek Sharma celebrates his hundred (AP/PTI) Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing a 35-ball century as India defeated New Zealand by six wickets in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. The left-handed opener hammered 113 off just 38 deliveries, striking 11 sixes and nine fours as India chased down New Zealand's target of 199 in only 13.2 overs, with 40 balls to spare. Sharma received explosive support from 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as the pair tore into the New Zealand attack from the outset. Jacob Duffy conceded 26 runs in the opening over, followed by 17 and 21 in the next two as India raced to 64 without loss in three overs. The onslaught intensified as India plundered 20 runs in the fourth over, 16 in the fifth and another 18 in the sixth to finish the Powerplay at a staggering 118 without losing a wicket. Sharma reached his fifty off just 15 balls. Matthew Fisher eventually broke the opening stand in the eighth over, dismissing Sooryavanshi for a blistering 45 off 19 deliveries, including four sixes and four fours. However, Sharma continued his assault alongside Sanju Samson, taking India to 156/1 after eight overs. After a relatively quiet ninth over, Sharma brought up his century off 35 balls against Kyle Jamieson in the 10th over. He eventually fell to Jamieson for 113 off 38 deliveries, but India were already firmly in control. The chase briefly lost momentum as Shreyas Iyer and Samson departed towards the end. India, however, comfortably crossed the finish line in 13.2 overs to register a commanding victory. Jamieson claimed two wickets, while Fisher and Mitchell Santner took one apiece. None of New Zealand's bowlers managed to keep their economy rate below 12 runs per over. Mitchell, Jacobs lift New Zealand to 198/3 Earlier, Daryl Mitchell 's unbeaten 89 off 52 balls helped New Zealand post 198/3 after India opted to bowl. Bevon Jacobs provided a brisk finish with 39 off 23 deliveries as the pair added an unbeaten 75-run stand for the fourth wicket. New Zealand lost Tim Seifert early, with Arshdeep Singh dismissing the opener for two. Finn Allen and Mitchell then rebuilt the innings, putting together 86 runs before Nitish Kumar Reddy removed Allen for 40 off 25 balls, an innings featuring five sixes. Glenn Phillips, playing his 100th T20I, could manage only 17 before Axar Patel dismissed him in the 12th over. Mitchell and Jacobs subsequently ensured the hosts finished with a competitive total, although India's bowlers restricted the scoring in the latter half of the innings. Arshdeep, Axar and Nitish picked up a wicket each, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar went wicketless. India rewrite the record books India's emphatic chase ranked among the quickest successful pursuits of a target of at least 190 in T20 cricket. Their 199-run chase, completed with 40 balls remaining, was second on the all-team list behind Estonia's successful pursuit of 192 against Cyprus in 2024, which left 42 balls unused. title: 'We don't play enough T20': Gautam Gambhir asks players to 'stay in shape' after New Zealand series
text: Gautam Gambhir India head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked his players to maintain their fitness and continue working on their game during a month-long break from T20I cricket after India completed a 3-2 series win over New Zealand. title: 'We were a bit sloppy': Shreyas Iyer points out India's mistakes after 5th T20I defeat against New Zealand
text: Shreyas Iyer reflects on India's defeat (Image: BCCI/X) India captain Shreyas Iyer admitted that his team fell short in all three departments after suffering a seven-wicket defeat against New Zealand in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. Despite clinching the five-match series 3-2, Iyer pointed to India's inability to maintain momentum with the bat, coupled with an underwhelming bowling and fielding display, as key reasons behind the defeat. India posted 191/8 after being asked to bat first, with Ishan Kishan and Iyer producing impressive half-centuries. However, the visitors failed to capitalise on their strong recovery after losing both set batters in quick succession. Watch Virat Kohli drives, edges but doesn't stop in Auckland | Exclusive visuals New Zealand made the most of India's shortcomings in the field and chased down the target in just 17.4 overs. Tim Seifert led the charge with a blistering 93 off 50 deliveries, while Glenn Phillips remained unbeaten on 65 off 38 balls to guide the hosts to a comfortable seven-wicket victory. Speaking at the post-match presentation, Iyer acknowledged that India could have done better after building a promising platform with the bat. "It was plausible, honestly. We could have been better considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I created the momentum. And then from there on we lost back-to-back wickets. And then suddenly pressure on the new batsman," Iyer said. Shreyas Iyer rues India's batting collapse after strong partnership Iyer and Kishan added 93 runs for the third wicket after India were reduced to 19/2 early in the innings. Kishan scored 61 off 32 balls, while the Indian skipper contributed 50 off just 23 deliveries. The duo helped India recover from a difficult position and put the visitors on course for a total in excess of 200. However, their dismissals in quick succession disrupted India's momentum and allowed New Zealand to regain control. Iyer also highlighted the nature of the surface, explaining how the movement and variable bounce made batting challenging, particularly against deliveries directed at a hard length. "It wasn't an easy wicket to play on, especially when the ball was seaming and holding a bit. And also skidding through at times. You must have seen a couple of us; Tilak and I got out in a similar fashion. So yeah, it was challenging, especially with that hard length. But to get to 194, yeah, it was reasonable, I feel. I think we still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. We were a bit sloppy," he added. Iyer admits India need to improve their fielding India's fielding lapses also proved costly during New Zealand's chase. Naman Dhir dropped Seifert when the opener was batting on 13, allowing him to make the most of the reprieve and go on to score a match-winning 93. Sanju Samson also missed an opportunity to dismiss Phillips after failing to hold on to a sharp outside edge in the 15th over. Iyer admitted that fielding remains an area where India need to improve, while acknowledging the challenges of playing under different conditions in New Zealand. But we can brainstorm, and we have to work on a couple of things, especially fielding. That is one aspect of the game we need to improve on," he said. "But honestly, it's not that easy when you come under such dark lights, clear skies. We don't get that much in India. But yeah, great learning curve," he added. title: 'I donât play this game to prove anyone wrong': Sanju Samson after India's 1st T20I win over New Zealand
text: Sanju Samson celebrates after scoring 50 runs during the T20 cricket international between New Zealand and India in Christchurch, New Zealand. India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has stressed the importance of trusting his process and staying focused on his game despite the criticism and opinions that come with playing for the national team. His comments came after India chased down 230/6 with two balls remaining to record their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the opening match of the five-game series. Samson said he does not play to silence critics. Instead, he focuses on his preparation, keeps things simple and avoids letting social media reactions affect his mindset. You have to stay committed to the process and create the right environment for yourself. Playing for Indian cricket is not easy, with so much noise and so many people having their own opinions. But I donât play this game with the mindset of proving anyone wrong. I keep my cricket at the forefront, trust my process, respect my practice and focus on doing the best I can. I like to keep things simple and stay focused on what I can control, rather than letting outside opinions influence my mindset,â Samson told reporters after the match. Gill's bowling attack faces big test ahead of NZ ODI series "Their breach was in accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement. title: 'It was just me and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': Abhishek Sharma after his record-breaking innings in India's 3rd T20I win over New Zealand
text: Abhishek Sharma Abhishek Sharma credited meticulous preparation and a clear game plan for his sensational century against New Zealand, revealing that he had âmanifestedâ the innings before producing a breathtaking performance in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday. The left-handed opener smashed 113 off just 38 balls, helping India chase down 199 in only 13.2 overs. The six-wicket victory gave India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. Abhishek and teenage opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who scored 45 off 19 deliveries, combined to register a record-breaking 118 without loss in the powerplay, the highest total recorded in the first six overs of a men's T20 international. It was just me and Vaibhav, just going to enjoy there for a bit, especially in the powerplay,â he told broadcasters. The Indian opener said the duo assessed the pitch while fielding and identified opportunities to exploit Wellington's short square boundaries and the pace of New Zealand's bowlers. âEspecially when we were fielding, we were observing the pitch a bit because of this extra bounce. But I feel the dimensions of the ground, we could use the powerplay, and we could use their pace as well. So that was the easy plan,â he added. Preparation behind the explosive innings Abhishek stressed that such performances are rarely accidental, highlighting the work he puts in during training and the support he receives from India's coaching staff. âI feel it's not that, I wouldn't say it's that easy, but it's just the preparation behind the scenes. Special mention to our coaches because of the sidearms; we've been playing them a lot,â he said. The batter explained that understanding the conditions and adapting to the opposition's bowling plans were central to his approach. âPreparation is really important as a batter. If you see the conditions and the dimensions, that's always in your mind, and then you have to keep the bowlers also in your mind and play the shots according to the bowlers,â Abhishek said. After revealing that India had enjoyed a productive training session the previous day, he described how the performance matched his expectations. âWe had a good practice session yesterday, and I just wanted to utilise it, and that's what I did. Abhishek reached his half-century in just 15 balls before completing his hundred in 35 deliveries, making the innings one of the standout performances of his T20 career. title: 'That monkey's still on my back': Tim Seifert rues missed century, hails Glenn Phillips' stunning form against India
text: New Zealand's Tim Seifert (AP/PTI Photo) Tim Seifert came agonisingly close to ending his wait for a maiden international century, falling seven runs short after a blistering 93 in New Zealand's seven-wicket victory over India in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. But while the opener was disappointed at missing out on the milestone, he was happier that New Zealand finished the series with a win, even if their late revival came too late to prevent India from clinching the series 3-2. Seifert, who had endured a difficult series with four successive single-digit scores, produced a stunning turnaround in the final match, smashing 93 off just 50 deliveries. He was dropped on 13 before making India pay with an aggressive innings that put New Zealand firmly on course to chase down 192 in just 18 overs. However, his hopes of a maiden international hundred ended when he played a back-of-a-length delivery from Nitish Kumar Reddy onto his stumps, leaving him seven short of the landmark. Watch Tim Seifert on New Zealand's comeback, India's bowling & Glenn Phillips' record breaking series Speaking after the match, Seifert joked that the wait for his first international century continued to weigh on him. "No, look, the main thing is to win. But at the same time, you know, that monkey's still on my back for getting my first International 100. So look, you're still a little bit devastated about that. And I think my shoulders and back are getting a bit heavier as well," he joked. "But no, I think the main thing is winning. And that's the great thing. "But at the end of the day as well, you sometimes got to get over the line, especially because I haven't got one before. So yeah, hopefully it doesn't take another 95 games to get that opportunity. But we'll see what happens," Seifert added. Seifert explains New Zealand's late turnaround The opener said adapting to different conditions and learning from mistakes in the earlier matches were crucial to New Zealand's improved performances towards the end of the series. "Yeah, look, I think you've got to be true to yourself. You know, you can fall into a bit of T20 cricket. But you know, you still got to be tough on yourself about playing high-quality shots, high-percentage shots for you. "Yes, you want to put pressure on the bowlers. But you know, sometimes you can get a bit ahead of yourself and try to go too hard. I think you still got to adapt to the wicket that you play on. "So you play in India, you play in New Zealand, two completely different wickets. So no matter where you play in the world, you just got to adapt to what you're playing on. Some will be easier to play shots early; some you might have to wait until the back end of the powerplay." New Zealand had lost the first three matches before registering victories in the final two. Seifert felt the hosts had been competitive in the opening encounters but failed to seize crucial moments. "Yeah, I think it was the learning from the previous games. You know, we were close in Christchurch (1st and 2nd T20Is). It's just about winning those little margins when the game is on the line. I think the bowlers, the batters have stepped up and adapted to the wickets that we've played on," he said. "Look, that's (winning) your main goal at the start of the series. But when you look back at the series, I think we played good cricket in Christchurch. We just didn't win the final moments." He added: "Walking away from Christchurch, you know, we could have easily been 2-0 up or at least 1-all. So, I think, you know, these last two games especially have just kind of put the nail in the coffin about, you know, those final moments that we didn't quite nail in the first two games." 'Take a hat off to him': Seifert on Phillips' record-breaking series While Seifert provided the fireworks in the final match, Glenn Phillips was the standout performer across the series. The middle-order batter finished with 341 runs, breaking Phil Salt 's record of 331 runs for the most runs by a batter in a bilateral T20I series. Phillips' remarkable run included scores of 82 not out, 70, 17, 107 and an unbeaten 65 in the final match. He also became one of only three batters to register four or more half-centuries in a bilateral T20I series. Seifert praised his teammate's consistency and the way he built his innings rather than going after the bowlers from the outset. title: Naman Dhir makes his mark on maiden overseas tour, wins India's Impact Player of the Series medal
text: Naman Dhir (Pic credit: BCCI) NEW DELHI: Naman Dhir made a memorable start to his international career overseas, earning the Impact Player of the Series medal after playing a key role in India's 3-2 T20I series victory against New Zealand. title: Arshdeep Singh on the verge of scripting history, set to become first Indian to achieve this feat
text: India's Arshdeep Singh (PTI Photo) Arshdeep Singh is on the verge of creating history as India prepare for their five-match T20I series against New Zealand, with the left-arm pacer needing just five more wickets to become the first Indian bowler to reach 150 wickets in the format. The series begins on Thursday, with the opening T20I scheduled to be played in Christchurch. Arshdeep is expected to be an important part of India's plans across the five matches after recovering from a shoulder blow sustained during the fourth T20I against the West Indies. He was included in the playing XI for the fifth T20I in Bengaluru, although that match was washed out by rain. Since making his T20I debut in 2022, Arshdeep has established himself as one of India's leading bowlers in the shortest format. He became the country's highest T20I wicket-taker at the start of 2025 and has continued to add to his tally. In 99 T20Is, the Punjab Kings pacer has claimed 145 wickets at an average of 20.30. His record includes two four-wicket hauls and a five-wicket haul, with best figures of 5/51. Five more wickets would make Arshdeep the ninth bowler overall to reach 150 T20I wickets and the first Indian to achieve the feat. Afghanistan's Rashid Khan currently leads the all-time list with 197 wickets in 118 matches. Arshdeep has already enjoyed success against New Zealand, taking 17 wickets in 10 T20Is at an average of 20.00. His tally against the Black Caps includes a four-wicket haul and a five-wicket haul, with his best figures of 5/51. In New Zealand, he has picked up four wickets in two T20Is. His best performance on Kiwi soil came in Napier in 2022, where he returned figures of 4/37. title: 'Not good news': Ex-India star questions India's handling of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP Photo) Former India batter Mohammad Kaif has questioned India's decision to leave Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out of the fourth T20I against New Zealand. He believes the young batter should have been given another opportunity, especially after India had already secured the series. Sooryavanshi played the second and third T20Is after Ishan Kishan was ruled out due to injury. However, when Kishan returned to the team, the youngster had to make way for him in the fourth match, which India lost. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more Kaif feels that giving Sooryavanshi a consistent run would have helped build his confidence. He also pointed out that India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead before the fourth match. "Not good news for Sooryavanshi" Kaif believes that leaving out a young player after giving him just two opportunities is not the right approach. "This is not good news for the player (not getting a consistent run). He is a potential superstar. And you have seen what he can do. In the third T20I, he and Abhishek Sharma scored 100 runs in six overs. For his confidence-building, it is not good news for any player, even if he is a veteran," Kaif said on his YouTube channel. He felt the fourth T20I was the right opportunity to give Sooryavanshi another game, as India had already won the series. "There was an opportunity to play him in this game. You had already won the series. You need to see the situation you are in during the series. On one side, you left Bhuvneshwar out and said you would bring in new players. Vaibhav is also new, so why not give him the same treatment? You are grooming Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav. By the same logic, he should have played. The platform was well set." Will Sooryavanshi get another chance in the fifth T20I? India will look to make a few changes when they face New Zealand in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. India lead the series 3-1 but suffered a heavy 87-run defeat in Auckland in the fourth match. The result could prompt the team management to make changes to its playing XI. Sooryavanshi is among the players who could return to the side. Sanju Samson could make way for the youngster after struggling for runs in the series. The final match could give Sooryavanshi another opportunity to impress as India look to finish the series with a victory. title: Sanju Samson's blazing 67 sets up India's record T20I chase against New Zealand
text: Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma There were concerns around the Indian team being jetlagged when it arrived at Christchurchâs Hagley Oval for the first T20I against New Zealand on Thursday. After all, the team were involved in a T20I series-decider vs West Indies in Bengaluru last Saturday. By the end of the Powerplay in Indiaâs innings, however, it was the hosts who looked dazed as Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma unleashed another of their trademark assaults in pursuit of 226. Samsonâs dazzling 67 off 33 balls laid the foundation for Indiaâs highest successful T20I chase, with Naman Dhirâs unbeaten 42 off 15 balls sealing a four-wicket victory with two deliveries to spare. Watch Sitanshu Kotak Press Conference: Update on Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav in Playing XI and more There is a striking simplicity to the way Samson and Abhishek go about their business. Compulsively, they seem to challenge the 100-run mark in the Powerplay. Scoring at least 80-plus, now seems routine. On Thursday, it was Samson who led the charge as India raced to 94/1 in six overs, with Abhishek contributing a brisk 29 off 12 before falling off the penultimate ball of the Powerplay. The significance and impact of Samsonâs knock extended beyond just the runs. It bought valuable time for captain Shreyas Iyer to assess the large boundaries and rebuild after India stumbled against Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell. From 93 without loss, India slipped to 122/4, briefly allowing New Zealand to get back into the contest. The hosts hardly helped themselves. Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson struggled for control, conceding 16 wides, while New Zealand also shelled three catches. By then, Samson and Abhishek had already shaken the home sideâs confidence. Every one of Samsonâs eight fours and four sixes seemed to drive a dagger in their hearts and hopes. Indiaâs T20 blueprint is now well established. Their openers are encouraged to attack relentlessly, irrespective of the target. âEven if we are chasing 170 and weâve got off to a flyer, we make sure we kill the game in the Powerplay itself. Thatâs what weâve been doing really well in the last couple of years,â Samson said after the match. title: Glenn Phillips scripts history, breaks Phil Salt's world record in stunning T20I series against India
text: New Zealand's Glenn Phillips (AP Photo) NEW DELHI: Glenn Phillips signed off a remarkable five-match T20I series against India by rewriting the record books, becoming the highest run-scorer in a bilateral series in the format. The New Zealand batter surpassed England's Phil Salt, whose previous record had stood since 2023, during the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. Phillips went past Salt's tally of 331 runs, scored against the West Indies in 2023, when he reached 332 during his unbeaten innings against India. He eventually finished with 341 runs in the series, establishing a new benchmark for the most runs scored in a bilateral T20I series. Watch Rohit Sharma faces tough challenge in Auckland nets The right-hander continued his extraordinary consistency with an unbeaten 65 off 38 balls in the final match, helping New Zealand chase down India's target of 192 with seven wickets and 12 balls to spare. Phillips finished the series with scores of 82 not out, 70, 17, 107 and 65 not out, registering three half-centuries and a century. He also became only the third batter to record four 50-plus scores in a bilateral T20I series, joining Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan and Japan's S Ravichandran. Four 50+ scores in a bilateral T20I series Mohd Rizwan vs Eng 2022 S Ravichandran (Japan) vs Mongolia 2024 G Phillips vs Ind 2026 Glenn Phillips surpasses Phil Salt in elite list Salt had held the previous record with 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023. Pakistan's Rizwan occupies the third position with 316 runs against England in 2022, while Estonia's Sahil Chouhan (297 against Cyprus in 2024) and New Zealand's Mark Chapman (290 against Pakistan in 2023) complete the top five. Phillips' consistency was central to New Zealand's batting campaign, with his ability to accelerate against both pace and spin making him a major threat throughout the series. He was named Player of the Series for his outstanding contribution. Speaking after the match, Phillips credited his composure and approach, saying he enjoyed going out to bat with the mindset of being the hunter rather than the prey. He also highlighted the importance of attacking India's spin bowling, particularly Varun Chakravarthy, whose overs presented a crucial phase during the chase. Most runs in a bilateral T20I series 341* - G Phillips vs Ind 2026 331 - P Salt vs WI 2023 316 - Mohd Rizwan vs Eng 2022 297 - Sahil Chouhan (Estonia) vs Cyprus 2024 290 - M Chapman vs Pak 2023 Tim Seifert, Phillips power New Zealand to series-ending win While Phillips finished the series with another unbeaten half-century, opener Tim Seifert was the standout performer in the final match, producing a brilliant 93 to put New Zealand firmly in control of the chase. India had posted 191/8 after being asked to bat first by New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner. Ishan Kishan led the recovery with 61 off 32 balls, while Shreyas Iyer contributed 50 off just 23 deliveries. The pair shared a century partnership after India lost early wickets, but Adam Milne's outstanding spell of 4/19 restricted the visitors from making a bigger total. New Zealand lost Finn Allen early in the chase but Seifert steadied the innings and took the attack to the Indian bowlers. He shared a 73-run partnership with Daryl Mitchell before combining with Phillips for an 86-run stand for the third wicket. title: 'It's not easy to let go of  batting position': Abhishek Sharma hails Sanju Samson's sacrifice for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

title: 'Vaibhav Sooryavanshi needs to wait': Ex-India cricketer wants youngster dropped after just one innings
text: India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP/PTI) Former India batter Subramaniam Badrinath has suggested that India bring Varun Chakaravarthy back into the playing XI for the third T20I against New Zealand, rather than continue with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi at No. 3. India can seal the series with a win in Wellington on Tuesday after taking a 2-0 lead in the first two matches. Sooryavanshi was brought into the side for the second T20I after Ishan Kishan was ruled out with an injury. New Zealand's scores of 220 and 180 could have been 200 and 160 in the first two games," Badrinath said on his YouTube channel, Cric it with Badri. Varun has been out of action for India since suffering an abdominal side strain during last month's T20I series against Afghanistan. title: Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson set for scans after injury concerns hit New Zealand ahead of 3rd T20I
