title: Haris Rauf punished for on-field confrontation during Pakistan's  win over England
text: Haris Rauf fined for heated exchange with Will Jacks Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been fined 20 per cent of his match fee and received a demerit point for his on-field behaviour during Sunday's ODI against England in Lahore. The visitors were also penalised after failing to maintain the required over-rate. The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed that Rauf breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which covers conduct contrary to the spirit of the game. He received an official reprimand, taking his tally to five demerit points following his third offence within a 24-month period. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more The incident occurred towards the end of Pakistan's innings, after the 46th over, when Rauf was at the non-striker's end. The pacer appealed for a wide before getting into an argument with England all-rounder Will Jacks . Rauf raised his bat during the exchange and continued the argument despite being warned by umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid. He then brushed past the umpire while moving towards Jacks. England were handed a separate penalty, with their players fined 15 per cent of their match fees for maintaining an over-rate three overs below the required level, even after time allowances were taken into account. The sanction was imposed under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which provides for a five per cent fine on players' match fees for every over a team falls short of the minimum over-rate requirement. Both Rauf and England captain Harry Brook accepted the charges and the penalties proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees. As a result, neither case required a formal hearing. The charges against the two teams were brought by on-field umpires Rashid Riaz and Sharfuddoula, third umpire Wayne Knights and fourth umpire Nassir Hussain. title: âI think about going for a boundary off the very first ballâ: Tilak Varma on his new role for India
text: Tilak Varma (ANI Photo) India vice-captain Tilak Varma says his move from No. 3 to the middle order has brought a shift in his batting approach, with the left-hander now looking to attack from the outset whenever the opportunity presents itself. Tilak, who has established himself as a reliable performer in run chases over the past 12 months, has adapted to batting at No. 5 or 6 by balancing his attacking instincts with the need to take the game deep. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more "I already had the power game; I have scored runs at number three as well. Now, batting at number five or six, I think about going for a boundary off the very first ball only if it's there to be hit," he said ahead of the fourth T20I against New Zealand. "Otherwise, I focus on taking the game deep. I take a bit more time. Initially, I focus on singles and doubles, finding gaps for fours or two runs," he added. The approach has served him well, including during India's tense chase in the second T20I against New Zealand, when he combined with Nitish Kumar Reddy to guide the team through a difficult situation. India have since taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. âThe bowler is under far more pressureâ Tilak believes managing the pressure on bowlers is an important part of his approach during the closing stages of a chase. Rather than allowing the situation to dictate his decisions, he tries to remind himself that the bowler is the one facing greater pressure. "In the end overs, as a batsman, the bowler is under far more pressure than I am. That positive thought is constantly running in my head, that the bowler is under more pressure, so they are bound to leak runs." Recalling his crucial partnership with Reddy at Hagley Oval, Tilak said he encouraged his batting partner to remain at the crease and keep the chase alive rather than worry about the result. "I just told Nitish, 'if we pull the match off from here, it's going to be immense fun. Let's just stay out there, take the game deep, and see what happens'." India eye 5-0 series sweep Despite having already clinched the series, India are not planning to ease off in the remaining matches. Tilak said the team wants to make the most of the opportunity to complete a clean sweep. "We are thinking this is a great opportunity to achieve a clean sweep. The next goal is to win the upcoming match and give the Indian crowd a great chance to witness a 5â0 series win." Tilak acknowledged that adapting to different conditions and a new time zone was challenging, but insisted that the players could not use it as an excuse. "At this level, we cannot make excuses. We are at the highest level, and we need to set standards for the youngsters who look up to us. "Gautam sir (head coach Gautam Gambhir) made it clear in team meetings that this is a long tour and the standard we set as a T20 side will provide momentum for the ODI and Test squads," added Tilak. With the T20I series already secured, India will look to maintain their momentum and carry the same standards into the remaining fixtures of the New Zealand tour. title: Amid Vaibhav Sooryavanshi debate, Gautam Gambhir says, 'my job is not to make everyone happy'
text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Gautam Gambhir India head coach Gautam Gambhir said his responsibility was to make the right decisions for the team rather than please everyone, stressing that players who have performed consistently deserve a longer run. India have plenty of options on the bench, with teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi still waiting for an opportunity despite his performances. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma have continued to open the innings and played key roles in India's successful defence of their T20I World Cup title earlier this year. Watch Virat Kohli drives, edges but doesn't stop in Auckland | Exclusive visuals "First of all, my job is not to make everyone happy. My job is to take the right decisions, not the popular decisions. And that is what I'm there for," Gambhir told the broadcasters ahead of the fifth T20I against New Zealand on Sunday. He said maintaining a sense of security within the dressing room was important and that players who had delivered over a longer period should be backed. "No, it is very easy to take the popular decision. But for me, I think the important thing is to take the right decision and make sure that there is a lot of security inside the dressing room. "Because, as you just mentioned, there's a lot of talent. But again, I think guys who have done phenomenally well over a longer period of time obviously deserve a longer rope. And that is exactly how we approach the series." India had already sealed the five-match series against New Zealand by winning the first three games. Asked how he planned to keep the players motivated with the series decided, Gambhir said representing the country should be motivation enough. "When you're playing for your country, there is no complacency." "You've obviously got to remember that it's an international game. Everyone knows how few privileged players get the opportunity to represent the country. For me, every game is an opportunity to do something different, to learn something, to evolve. title: Abki baar 400 paar: India unleash six-hitting assault, set new world record in 2026
text: Abhishek Sharma India became the first team in cricket history to hit 400 sixes in a calendar year during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The milestone came in India's 40th match of 2026, when the batters struck 11 sixes to take their tally for the year to exactly 400. The previous record belonged to Austria, who hit 326 sixes in 2025. title: âNo reason to write him offâ: Ajinkya Rahane urges patience with Bhuvneshwar Kumar after tough return
text: India's Bhuvneshwar Kumar (AP/PTI photo) Ajinkya Rahane has backed Bhuvneshwar Kumar despite the experienced pacer's expensive return to international cricket, urging critics not to judge him too harshly after three difficult outings in the ongoing T20I series against New Zealand. Bhuvneshwar conceded 49, 50 and 40 runs across his first three matches, managing just one wicket. While he showed glimpses of his ability to generate swing with the new ball, the veteran pacer appeared short of rhythm in other phases of the game. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more However, Rahane believes a few below-par performances should not overshadow Bhuvneshwar's experience or his determination to make a comeback in Indian colours. âI donât think we should judge him or overthink how he has bowled. He is an experienced player and would certainly reflect on where he fell short and what he could have done better. As far as his performances are concerned, ups and downs are part of the game. Sometimes, as a bowler, you may not find your rhythm, but that is no reason to write him off. Bhuvneshwar Kumar would certainly know what he could have done better,â Rahane said on his YouTube channel. 'We should learn from this' Rahane said Bhuvneshwar's return itself deserved recognition, adding that the pacer should be appreciated for continuing to work towards representing India rather than being written off after a difficult series. âFor me, the biggest story is that he has made a comeback at this age. We should learn from this that, as a bowler, you must never give up. Keep doing your job, and things will eventually fall into place. You never know; he could take five wickets in the next match, and things could change immediately. Bhuvneshwar is a bowler who certainly reflects on his game, but he is also confident in his abilities and is a confident person overall,â he said. Bhuvneshwar has had some success with the new ball during the series, but his struggles to contain the opposition have come against the backdrop of increasingly batter-friendly T20 cricket. India's dominance with the bat has underlined the challenge facing bowlers in the format. title: Tilak Varma, the new chasemaster in town
text: Tilak Varma. (ANI Photo) Tilak Varma quietly slips into beast mode when he has a tricky chase to finish in T20Is. What Virat Kohli did against Pakistan in the T20 World Cup in Melbourne in 2022 is firmly embedded in the formatâs folklore. Over the past year, Tilak has been building his own legacy as someone capable of conjuring similar brilliance to haul his team out of trouble. Saturday night in Christchurch, on a two-paced Hagley Oval pitch against a wily New Zealand attack, provided another example of Tilakâs unflinching temperament and supreme skill in crunch situations. Coming out to bat in the 11th over with the scoreboard reading 69/4, he crafted an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls to guide India to their 181-run target with four wickets and a ball to spare. Watch Nitish Kumar Reddy on Tilak Varma partnership, batting under pressure & all-rounder role His unbroken seventh-wicket partnership of 69 off 30 balls with Nitish Kumar Reddy (26 not out off 13) not only secured India a 2-0 lead in the five-match series but also vindicated the team managementâs persistence with a capable batter at No. 8. This was a standout run chase for a simple reason. It was far removed from the run-fests of modern-day T20 cricket. It demanded skill to tackle left-arm spinner Mitchell Santnerâs exceptional spell of 4/21, awareness of the large boundaries and unwavering belief when India were 112/6, with the ball still playing tricks. Naman Dhirâs threatening 17-ball 31 had kept India in contention, but after his departure, another wicket could well have settled the contest in New Zealandâs favour. Tilakâs six fours and solitary six came just when India needed them. It helped that New Zealand carried their sloppy fielding over from the opening game two days earlier. As on Thursday, another special knock from Glenn Phillips â 70 off 43 balls in the hostsâ 180/5 â was overshadowed by Indiaâs young brigade. Most of these New Zealand players have seen Indiaâs young T20 batters pull off outrageous feats in the IPL. Perhaps some of the home teamâs nervousness in the field stemmed from those memories. Tilak, though, credited head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak. âGautam sir and Kotak sir said that whole India believes in you and that if I bat till the end, we can win,â Tilak said after the win. The clarity with which he structures a chase is almost unnerving. Against spin, the emphasis was on finding gaps and running hard. âI was telling Naman that we will push hard when the spinners are bowling. Unfortunately, Naman got out in Mitchellâs last over. Otherwise, we could have won in the 18th,â Tilak declared. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Dhirâs dismissal did little to unsettle Tilak. The plan remained the same when Reddy, the last recognised batter, walked out. They resisted the temptation to clear the ropes as they might on smaller grounds in India, instead working the gaps and running hard to turn ones into twos. The big shots could wait for the pace bowlers at the death. This generation of IPL batters is wired in such a way that no chase seems improbable until the equation demands a six off every ball, with the final over still to come. The panic button doesnât seem to exist. Tilak and Reddy lived up to that billing. They took the game deep and, even with 46 required off the last three overs, backed themselves. Seventeen runs off the 18th over and 18 off the 19th brought the equation down to 11 off six. Reddyâs winning two off the penultimate ball completed another escape. title: Hardik Pandyaâs heir: Can Nitish Reddy be a ready option for India?
text: India's Nitish Kumar Reddy (AP/PTI) That Nitish Kumar Reddy was one of only two players picked across all three squads for Indiaâs tour of New Zealand speaks volumes about how highly the team management rates him. For his part, the 25-year-old has done enough to justify the faith reposed in him. Reddy bowled his full quota in the opening T20I in Christchurch and was entrusted with the crucial 19th over. He conceded 12 runs in it and finished with a joint-best economy rate of 10 alongside Mayank Yadav. The trust remained intact in the second T20I. Reddy remained unbeaten on 26 off 13 deliveries, and his six off Jacob Duffy in the 17th over started Indiaâs march to victory. Those performances underlined his steady development as a genuine allrounder. Recognising his potential, the team management has preferred him ahead of Shivam Dube since the third T20I against the West Indies. While he is not yet in the same bracket as Pandya, whose all-round skill set remains unmatched in India, Reddy has age on his side and continues to make strides with both bat and ball. title: Will Ishan Kishan's injury be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's gain? 15-year-old in contention for 2nd T20I vs New Zealand
text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (BCCI Photo) One game into Indiaâs tour of New Zealand and the familiar fitness concerns have already surfaced. Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during the series opener on Thursday. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak revealed that Ishan was pushed down the order in the first T20I because of the injury. Watch Shreyas Iyer press conference: On Sanju Samson v Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and more Sooryavanshi attended an optional training session on Friday alongside Abhishek Sharma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Varun Chakravarthy, Shivam Dube and Kuldeep Yadav. Under Kotakâs watchful eye, he spent considerable time in the nets, a clear indication that the team wants him ready if needed. If the team management decides to veer away from their template of playing eight batters and field a spinner, Sooryavanshi may have to wait. Few young cricketers in recent years have generated as much excitement a s Sooryavanshi. His exploits in the IPL and age-group cricket have fuelled expectations, with fans, experts and social media all eager to see him in India colours more regularly. Yet the management feels patience will benefit him more than premature exposure. The challenge in New Zealand will be significantly different: larger grounds, movement off the pitch and through the air, and a minuscule margin for error. text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi with the fan After a smashing win against New Zealand, Indiaâs 15-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi was once again the centre of all the attention. In the video, now a viral sensation, she advised the teenage cricketer: âThanda paani mat peena, garam karke hi peenaâ (Don't drink cold water; warm it before drinking). Her concern about the cold New Zealand weather, delivered with the warmth of an elder speaking to a child from her own family. This sweet gesture turned an ordinary post-match interaction into a memorable moment. When a fan speaks like family The viral video also shows the woman informing him, âHum bhi Ballia se hainâ (We are also from Ballia). Itâs a town in Bihar and establishes a connection with the young batter who is also from Samastipur in Bihar. The young batsman also responded with a warm smile, âAchha ji, theek haiâ (Okay, all right). The video The interaction took place after India's third T20I against New Zealand on October 27, 2026, in Wellington. After the match, Vaibhav was signing a young spectatorâs cap and was interacting with fans. Among those was a woman who called out to him and introduced herself as someone from Ballia, Uttar Pradesh. What caught the attention of the Internet was rather than asking for an autograph or photograph, she offered advice that mothers would give their kids when they are away from home. With New Zealand's cold weather in mind, she tells him to avoid cold water. And drink it warm only. Her words were simple but were full of motherly concern which was extremely sweet and affectionate. Vaibhav listening, smiling and acknowledging her advice was too adorable to miss. The moment went viral because it was so cute and full of pure love which is rare. For a few seconds, the young international cricketer was not being treated like an international rising star. In that moment, he was only a young boy being reminded to take care of himself by an older woman who felt an emotional or regional connection with him. From a small village in Bihar to the international spotlight Vaibhav's Samastipur home Vaibhav's growing popularity is hardly surprising. Born on March 27, 2011, in Samastipur district of Bihar, the left-handed batter began learning cricket at a young age. He made his first-class debut for Bihar in January 2024, aged just 12 years and 284 days, and later became the youngest player to make an IPL appearance when he debuted for Rajasthan Royals in April 2025. The innings in New Zealand offered another reminder of his ability to change the momentum of a match in a matter of overs. Why this small interaction struck a chord The woman fanâs mention of Ballia gave the interaction a personal touch. She was not simply addressing a player she admired; she was expressing a sense of concern. Her advice about warm water reflected the everyday concern that people often show towards younger members of their community, particularly when they are far from home. Vaibhav's smile and brief response made the exchange feel natural rather than staged. There was no elaborate speech or grand gesture, just a fan expressing concern and a young cricketer acknowledging it. And perhaps that is what made the moment so relatable. title: Amol Muzumdar hints at specialist T20I squad for India women: 'Not long'
text: Amol Muzumdar Indian women's cricket team have been excellent in Test and ODI formats in recent times. Under former captain Harmanpreet Kaur , they won four of their last five Tests, a big feat considering that only four countries play Test cricket in the women's game. They are also the reigning Women's ODI World Cup champions, having clinched their maiden title almost exactly a year ago. However, their T20I game still needs improvement. India were knocked out in the league stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. In the shortest format, the team needs to improve on many fronts. Head coach Amol Muzumdar believes India could soon have a specialist T20I squad, similar to the men's team, with the next generation of cricketers better equipped to meet the demands of the format. Asked how soon that could become a reality, Muzumdar replied: âNot long.â Watch Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma and a lot of fun in Auckland âWeâre already on that path. Thereâs some amazing talent coming through. The talent Iâve seen at the CoE (Centre of Excellence), where they hold the India Under-15 and U-19 camps, is terrific. The work at the CoE is superb. The camps are a good reflection of where Indian womenâs cricket is at the moment. Iâm sure itâs in a healthy state,â he said at an event organised by the Sports Journalistsâ Association of Mumbai (SJAM) at the MIG Club on Saturday. Muzumdar believes the next generation could speed up that transition. Having grown up with the demands of modern T20 cricket, these players have a better understanding of the importance of nutrition, fitness and fielding. âThey are tuned in. They are professionals. Even the U-15 players are professionals. They understand the nutrition aspect of the game. They understand the fitness aspect of the game. They understand fielding. Theyâre terrific fielders. Theyâre good athletes. They understand that athleticism is key in cricket. Youâll soon find that when the younger generation takes over, India will be in a good state,â he said. The coach also said that a player's willingness to learn was as important to him as their skill. âI see whether he or she is receptive. If he or she is receptive, you know it from their body language. You need to learn to understand the body language of the player. Over the years, I have spent a few years in First-Class cricket, and I do understand that I can know a certain player through their body language on the ground. I try to catch those signals. There is always that correct timing of that advice that has to be given. So as a coach, you need to understand when to say, how to say and what to say,â he felt. Muzumdar said he was also conscious of giving players the space they needed. âSometimes you have to respect the space that the athlete wants. You can have 10,000 things as a coach to tell that athlete. But whether he or she is in that time frame or the mind frame to understand what you are doing...â he said. A year after India won their maiden Women's ODI World Cup title, beating South Africa in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai on November 2, Muzumdar recalled the team spirit that marked the campaign. He credited the unity within the squad and the atmosphere in the dressing room for helping the team during the tournament. âIf I have to pinpoint just one, then I think the unity in the camp and the dressing room atmosphere. Because of that unity, the dressing room atmosphere was very light. There was a little bit of a buzz around in the dressing room, which I love to create,â he said. Muzumdar compared that atmosphere to the Mumbai teams he played for in the 1990s, which won the Ranji Trophy several times during that period. âI have played in such teams where whenever we have done well, what I am talking about in the 90s, when we did well, just the dressing room atmosphere was phenomenal. There was some kind of a buzz triggered to the kind of cricket that was reflected on the ground. So I think if I have to pinpoint one, it is unity in the camp and just the buzz in the dressing room,â he said. Having worked closely with Harmanpreet during his three-year tenure, Muzumdar praised the outgoing captain and said he was looking forward to working with new skipper Smriti Mandhana . âI had a very good time with Harman as a captain. But Iâm also looking forward to the future. With utmost respect, the manner in which she conducted herself as a captain, as a skipper, was superb. I feel myself really lucky that I had that opportunity for the three years that I spent with her as a coach. I could gather the mindset of the captain... I could gather the mindset of the leader in her. I consider myself really lucky about it,â he said. title: Time for the victory lap: India aim to maintain unbeaten run in Auckland as New Zealand look to avoid whitewash
text: Abhishek Sharma The series is settled. Now it's time for some fun. Team India, the Harlem Globetrotters of world cricket, have continued their march through New Zealand, arriving from humid home conditions just a day before the series began and making it 3-0 in style over the course of just a week, which teams would normally use to acclimatise to foreign conditions. After the stupendous feasts the batters enjoyed on the drop-in pitches in Christchurch and Wellington, the focus shifts to unique Eden Park in Auckland, a ground originally built with rugby in mind. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more The straight boundaries here are probably only a little longer than your backyard, while the longer square boundaries will test the power of India's hitmen. New Zealand's bowlers will need the motivation to bend their backs after watching India chase 199 in 13.2 overs on Tuesday. The Black Caps are already hampered by the absence of experienced pacers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson, both sidelined by injury, and the Indian batters should be licking their lips. Ravi Shastri said on air the other day that a question he gets asked often in New Zealand is: "Will that 15-year-old play?" Wellington fans got a glimpse of the young sensation as he smashed a 19-ball 45 in the third game, an innings that, remarkably, played second fiddle to Abhishek Sharma's 38-ball 113. Sooryavanshi's opportunity came because of Ishan Kishan's injury, but Indian spin legend R Ashwin feels that if the Jharkhand batter returns to the XI, Sanju Samson should reclaim his opening slot and Vaibhav should miss out. His ability to generate incredible power against the short ball, along with his straight-hitting, should be enough for the team management to let the fun continue. If Gautam Gambhir and Co. are serious about testing the temperament and skill of the Indian pace attack, Eden Park should be an ideal venue. If the pitch remains a belter, as it often is in T20Is in New Zealand, the Indian quicks' ability to hit a hard length will be tested. title: Tilak Varma reveals Gautam Gambhir's message that inspired him during thrilling chase against New Zealand: 'Whole India believes in you'
text: India's coach Gautam Gambhir, right, Tilak Varma (PTI Photo) Tilak Varma revealed the special message he received from India head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak ahead of the second T20I against New Zealand, which proved instrumental in inspiring his match-winning performance in Christchurch on Saturday. Tilak produced an unbeaten 51 off just 26 deliveries to guide India to a remarkable four-wicket victory after the visitors found themselves in deep trouble during the 181-run chase. Nitish Kumar Reddy provided the perfect support with an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls as the duo stitched together an unbroken 69-run stand off just 30 deliveries to seal the win with one ball to spare. Watch Sitanshu Kotak Press Conference: Update on Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav in Playing XI and more 'Whole India believes in you' Named Player of the Match for his decisive knock, Tilak revealed that Gambhir and Kotak had backed him to take responsibility and finish the game if he remained at the crease. âJust before todayâs game, I was talking with coach Gautam sir and Sitanshu Kotak sir. I was talking with both of them, and they said one thing: âWe all believe, and the whole of India believes in you. If you stay till the end, then you will win the game for usâ,â Tilak said during the post-match presentation. The left-hander added that the message stayed with him when he walked out to bat amid India's collapse. Rather than chasing the target recklessly, he focused on taking the game deep and giving himself the best chance to finish the job. âSo thatâs what was going through my mind. I wanted to take the game as deep as possible, and at the end of the day, again, what everyone has believed and has done. So Iâm really proud of myself,â he added. âWeâll stay till the endâ: Tilak's message to Naman Dhir Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Tilak also explained how he approached the partnership with Naman, stressing the importance of staying at the crease and keeping the scoreboard moving on a surface that played slower than it had in the opening match. âI was telling Naman that weâll stay till the end, and especially the wicket was slightly slower today, compared to the last game. So, I was telling Naman that weâll push hard in running between the wickets when spinners were bowling,â he said. The approach reflected Tilak's patience during a challenging phase of the chase. Instead of allowing the rising required rate to force risky shots, he focused on building partnerships and preserving India's chances until the final overs. Tilak-Nitish partnership seals memorable comeback With India needing close to 70 runs in the final five overs and only four wickets remaining, the contest appeared to be New Zealand's side. Tilak's 51 not out included six fours and a six, while Nitish finished unbeaten on 26. title: Nitish Kumar Reddy strengthens his case as India's next pace-bowling allrounder
text: Nitish Kumar Reddy (AP/PTI) That Nitish Kumar Reddy, being one of only two players named in all three squads for the New Zealand tour, speaks volumes about how highly India rate his skills. It has also provided the team management with an opportunity to develop an alternative to the often-injured Hardik Pandya , who is not getting any younger. On his part, the 25-year-old has made useful contributions to justify the faith shown in him. Reddy bowled his full quota of four overs in the first T20I in Christchurch and was entrusted with the responsibility of delivering the 19th over. He conceded 12 runs in that over and finished with a joint-best economy rate of 10, alongside Mayank Yadav. In the second game, he was once again handed the ball in the 19th over. This time, he conceded just 14 runs and claimed a wicket. The right-hander later returned to stitch together an unbeaten 69-run partnership off 30 balls with Tilak Varma to steer India to victory from a difficult position. He finished unbeaten on 26 off 13 balls. Those two performances are a testament to his ever-improving skills as an allrounder. The team think tank has recognised his potential and has preferred him over Shivam Dube since the third T20I against the West Indies. While he cannot yet be put in the same league as Pandya, whose skill set remains superior to that of any other Indian allrounder, Reddy has age on his side and continues to improve both aspects of his game, besides being an excellent fielder. India bowling coach Morne Morkel believes Reddy has the skills to become the all-format allrounder India have been desperately searching for and one who could eventually emerge as Pandya's successor. Morkel recently backed him publicly, stating that he is a player to "keep an eye on" and someone capable of producing a "magical ball" to unsettle batters. Reddy, too, does not shy away from questions about his credentials as an allrounder, nor does he shy away from putting in hard yards. "The amount of work I have to do is more than anyone else, on and off the field," he said after the second game against New Zealand. Reddy made his Test debut during the 2024 tour of Australia and gave a good account of himself, including a century at the MCG against a bowling attack featuring Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines While he showed what he could do with the bat, his bowling lacked the much-needed zip required to cement a regular place in the XI as an allrounder. He addressed that shortcoming by working with Steffan Jones, a former county cricketer and now a fast-bowling and high-performance coach, shortly before the 2026 IPL. The results were there for everyone to see. His pace consistently touched the mid-130kph range, a significant improvement from the mid-120s he had been bowling before his sessions with Jones. Reddy's biggest challenge, however, remains his fitness. He was set to travel to Zimbabwe for his maiden India call-up after the 2024 T20 World Cup, but a hernia injury scuppered those plans. Since then, he has spent considerable time on the sidelines with various injuries, including a freak gym accident in which he injured his left knee. Earlier this year, a quadriceps injury also ruled him out of the UK tour. With Reddy improving with every outing, the onus is now on the team management to use him judiciously and keep him fit and ready for the bigger challenges that lie ahead. title: 'Some of the things hurt me': Zimbabwe captain slams players' 'complacency' after series loss as Afghanistan go from 5 for 4 to score 221
text: Sikandar Raza Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called "complacency" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat to Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The loss also handed Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Raza said his biggest concern was the attitude of some players after Zimbabwe had reduced Afghanistan to 5 for 4 in the fourth over. He felt the team had taken the opposition lightly at that stage, assuming Afghanistan would struggle to post a big total. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more "For me, before I go too much in detail [about the match] - and I will address that in the changing room - the toughest part to swallow was the complacency that I saw from some of the boys," Raza said after the match. The Zimbabwe captain was particularly unhappy that some players appeared to believe Afghanistan would manage only 130 or 140 runs after losing four wickets early. He said the team needed to stay focused and remember that a match is not over until the final ball. "[At 5 for 4] some of the boys were probably calculating that it will be - 130, 140 max - at the end of 20 overs. Some of the things that I saw on the ground today certainly hurt me and I'll address that in the changing room because, listen, it can happen but I think that's where you have to be mentally very strong and say, 'no, the game is never over until it's over - we still have a job in hand and I'm going to be the guy who's going to get the job done'. "Before I dissect the game with batting or bowling, I think that's something that I felt today out there in the middle and that's something that needs to be addressed, not to take this game for granted because it can bite back and today is a great example." Zimbabwe had also kept Afghanistan to 45 for 5 at the halfway stage of the innings. However, Azmatullah Omarzai 's 116 off 50 balls and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai's 52 off 27 deliveries helped Afghanistan recover and post 221 for 7. Raza then led Zimbabwe's fightback with an unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, but his effort was not enough to prevent defeat. He said he had tried to keep his emotions under control while batting after being unhappy with the team's approach in the first innings. title: IND vs NZ: India's T20 reboot begins amid travel fatigue, tight schedule and bowling concerns
text: BCCI Photo Itâs been barely 48 hours since India landed in Christchurch after taking a flight out of Bengaluru. Shreyas Iyer and his men will be forgiven for still being sleep-deprived and jet-lagged when they walk out at Hagley Oval for the first of five T20Is against New Zealand today. Indian cricketers are conditioned to relentless travel, but that does not make the grind any less demanding. The modern cricket calendar is shaped more by commercial interests and diplomatic necessities and less by sporting logic and priorities. This tour is a case study. Stretching over 43 days, the visit marks a century of sporting ties between India and New Zealand, a relationship that dates back to the great Major Dhyan Chand leading an Indian Army hockey team to the country in 1926. It also offers New Zealand crowds a rare chance to watch Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma when the five-match ODI series follows the T20Is from Nov 4. Watch Mitchell Santner press conference: Special plan for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, facing World champs India Beyond all the ceremonial details, the tour could provide clues about the direction that Indian cricket takes across the three formats. For the Indian cricket fan and an unforgiving media, large sections of which are digital, the strains of a packed schedule are rarely considered valid excuses for a dip in performance standards and middling results. One saw that during the difficult tours of Ireland and England earlier this year. For many fans, critics and pundits, a side that can win two successive World Cups in a fickle format like T20, just cannot lose. While the Test team has got a good chance to acclimatise, the T20I side has been on the treadmill, playing non-stop in different conditions and continents. Predictably, skipper Iyer downplayed the scheduling challenge. âWeâve done that in the past... Itâs fun at the same time to be travelling, playing and getting accustomed to new conditions. We just want to put the reasons aside and see how we plan to win,â he said on match-eve. The coming 10 days could prove revealing for both the captain and his team. Indiaâs T20 setup remains in transition, with the road ultimately leading to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand later that year. While the composition of the touring squads suggests the two-Test series remains a priority, the T20 side arrives carrying a degree of desperation. That was reflected in the decision to recall Bhuvneshwar Kumar . Discarded after the 2022 New Zealand tour, the veteran seamer, now nearing 37, has been drafted in to lend experience to a bowling attack that is still searching for options in the absence of the peerless Jasprit Bumrah . âBhuvi brings a lot of experience. We were lacking that... He has won the IPL in the last two years and knows how to dominate this format,â Iyer explained. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines The bigger question is whether India have done enough over the last two years to build bowling depth beyond Bumrah. Bhuvneshwarâs return can be looked at with a mixed lens. Yes, it is a vote of confidence in a trusted campaigner. Under Gautam Gambhir and the current selection panel, India largely embraced a perform-or-perish approach, often showing limited patience with senior players. The recall of Bhuvneshwar therefore feels like a tactical retreat, an attempt to steady a T20 ship that rocked violently during the UK tour earlier this year. Whether this small step back helps India take a significant leap forward is a question only the next fortnight can answer. title: 'He was a fish out of water': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's No. 3 role questioned after IND vs NZ 2nd T20I
text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Ravichandran Ashwin believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was uncomfortable batting at No. 3 in Indiaâs second T20I against New Zealand and feels the team management should reconsider his position. The teenage batter, who replaced the injured Ishan Kishan in the playing XI, managed just four runs off eight balls after coming in during the sixth over. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma continued to open, leaving Sooryavanshi to bat in an unfamiliar position. Speaking after the match in Christchurch, Ashwin described the youngster as a âmissâ but stressed that it was too early to judge him negatively. Watch Nitish Kumar Reddy on Tilak Varma partnership, batting under pressure & all-rounder role "That is a miss. For a young cricketer like Vaibhav, 'miss' is too early I think to say, but because I have only two options of a hit or a miss, he just found himself a little like a fish out of water. He kept going hard, kept going hard for the eight balls," he said. Ashwin felt Sooryavanshi needed guidance from an experienced batter while trying to settle into the unfamiliar role. He said a senior partner could have helped the youngster remain calm and focus on playing the ball more carefully. "It did not feel like he was ever timing the ball, and that is when you need a senior partner to walk down to him and say, 'Calm down, just hang in there, look to play close to your body, watch the ball better.' Sometimes, as a batter, all you need to be told is to watch the ball closer. You do miss that in all the action that happens around you. So I just felt like he was a fish out of water. Walking in during the sixth over is not his cup of tea," he explained. Ashwin suggested that if India want to play Sooryavanshi, Abhishek and Samson together, Samson should move to No. 3, a role he has previously performed for India. "Look, I think they played this combination before, and Sanju had to skip down to number three. If they are going to go with this combination, I am not too sure Vaibhav has got to bat at number three, but it is what it is. Today it was a miss for Vaibhav," Ashwin further said. Ashwin praises Indiaâs middle order Ashwin also praised Indiaâs middle order, particularly Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ramandeep Singh, for helping the team chase New Zealandâs total of 180. title: How Justin Tuckerâs 89.1% career accuracy compares with Harrison Butkerâs career-low 68.8% this season
text: The Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad after Harrison Butker went 11 of 16 on field goals, a career-low 68.8%. (Getty Images) The Kansas City Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday, days after Harrison Butker missed two field goals in a loss at Seattle. Butker has made 11 of 16 attempts this season, a career-low 68.8%. Tucker, 36, owns an 89.1% career rate, second best in NFL history, but he has not kicked in the league since 2024. The Chiefs are 5-1, and head coach Andy Reid has not handed the job to anyone else. Still, a seven-time Pro Bowler now stands a few yards away from the man he might replace. Justin Tucker's 89.1% career rate against Butker's 68.8% this season Justin Tucker's number comes from a long stretch of work. Across 13 seasons in Baltimore he led the league at 94.6% in 2021 and posted a career-best 97.4% in 2016. His 417 made field goals rank 14th all time. He also once held the NFL record with a 66-yarder against Detroit. That is what a team is buying when it wants certainty. Butker's 68.8% is a different kind of figure. It covers only six games, so one clean weekend could move it a lot. But the drop is steep. He made 86.8% in 2025 and 88.4% from 2017 through 2025. This year he sits almost 20 points below his own norm. Butker began the season third all time, behind Tucker and Cameron Dicker. Now he is working against his own record. The sample is small enough that a recovery is still possible, but the Chiefs have seen enough to buy some insurance. Seattle showed the problem Sunday night made it plain. Butker missed a 58-yard field goal at the end of the first half and a 45-yarder in the fourth quarter. Kansas City lost 20-3, so every point mattered. A 58-yarder is a long try for anyone. The 45-yarder is the one that should bother the Chiefs. He has also missed an extra point this year, and NBC Sports counts seven misses across his last 11 games. Reid did not dodge it afterward. "He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football." He added that Butker is a bit off and has to fix it. Butker has three Super Bowl rings in Kansas City. That history buys patience. Why Justin Tucker is on the practice squad Tucker is not on the 53-man roster, and Butker's job is not in immediate danger. The Chiefs are 5-1, which gives them room to wait. They worked out three kickers this week and picked Tucker over former Rams kicker Harrison Mevis. The rÃ©sumÃ© comes with questions. In 2024 Tucker went 22 of 30, or 73.3%, the worst season of his career. The NFL then suspended him for 10 games in 2025, and the Ravens released him in May of that year. Tucker has maintained that he did nothing inappropriate. Workouts followed with the Saints, Colts and Jets, but no contract. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines So the Chiefs are weighing a proven career against a rough last season and a long layoff. If Butker misses again, they will not have to start a search. Practice squad players can also be elevated for game days, so a switch would not take much paperwork. title: 'Bowler can control the game': Bhuvneshwar Kumar on T20 cricket's batting boom and six-hitting revolution
text: Bhuvneshwar Kumar (Image: IANS) With T20 cricket increasingly defined by aggressive batting, shorter boundaries and relentless scoring, the margin for error for bowlers has become slimmer than ever. However, veteran India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes that quality bowling and adaptability can still make a decisive difference, insisting that the format is not entirely tilted in favour of batters. The 36-year-old, who has returned to India's international setup after nearly four years, shared his views following India's victory in the third T20I. Bhuvneshwar earned his comeback on the back of impressive performances in the IPL, where he has adapted his skills to meet the evolving demands of the shortest format. Watch Devdutt Padikkal Interview: India's No.3 opens up on Perth, Sri Lanka and preps for New Zealand 'A bowler can control the game' "I know that the margin of error is very low, which we generally talk about. But still, a bowler can land the ball wherever he wants to. I strongly believe that a bowler can control the game," Bhuvneshwar told reporters. Bhuvneshwar acknowledged that modern T20 cricket offers several advantages to batters, including smaller boundaries and an increasingly aggressive approach. However, he maintained that bowlers who execute their plans and adapt quickly can still dictate the course of a match. "This is a debatable question. We say that the conditions favour the batters nowadays and all that, but I still believe that a bowler can control the game. The reason is that we feed the ball to the batter," he said. "There are small boundaries. Everything is given to the batters. But still, a bowler is the one who feeds the ball to the batter. Then it's up to the batter what he wants to play, whether he wants to play according to the ball or not." "But still, if you look at the good bowlers, they are still doing well. They are consistent. Even if the game is not equal, the bowler adapts quickly. We've seen it in IPL, we've seen it here as well," he added. Bhuvneshwar not looking too far ahead after India comeback Despite returning to the international setup after a prolonged absence, Bhuvneshwar is not looking too far ahead in his career. The experienced pacer said he intends to continue playing domestic cricket and focus on performing consistently rather than setting long-term international targets. "It is great to be playing for India again but I am not thinking too much about the future. I will continue to play domestic cricket, whether it is Mushtaq Ali or Vijay Hazare," he said. Bhuvneshwar also credited his performances in the IPL over the past two years for opening the door to his return, adding that he had not actively chased an India comeback even though representing the country had always remained his dream. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines "I did not chase this (playing for India again) though it was always the dream. Credit goes to my performances in the IPL over the past two years," he added. 'Batters are looking to hit every ball' Bhuvneshwar also highlighted the changing mindset of batters, noting that modern players are increasingly unwilling to ease off even after scoring quickly at the start of an over. He recalled how batters previously tended to consolidate after striking a few boundaries, whereas the current generation continues to attack throughout the innings. "Earlier, somewhere there was a thinking that as runs have come in the first couple of balls, let's go easy in the remaining over. But now it is not like that. Batters are looking to hit every ball," he said. "There is one ball. There are two balls. There are six balls. Credit should be given to this generation for playing fearlessly," Bhuvneshwar added. title: Rouse Avenue court seeks Delhi Police response on Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea
text: Former JNU professor and Congress MP Bimol Akoijam (PTI file photo) NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue Court on Tuesday issued notice to Delhi Police on the anticipatory bail plea of Manipur MP and former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Bimol Akoijam in a sexual harassment case and extended his interim protection till November 5. Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought the police response and directed the investigating agency to place on record the complaint filed by JNU students against Akoijam. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5. Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station following allegations of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him when he was working as a professor at the university. During the hearing, Akoijam's counsel submitted that the complaint was made by a group of students to the dean and not by any aggrieved woman directly. The counsel also said the university's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) had examined the matter and its report had been annexed to the bail application. The defence further submitted that Akoijam had cooperated with the investigation and appeared before the investigating officer, while the alleged complainant was not joining the probe. title: 'Ball was seaming when Sanju and I went in': Shreyas Iyer calls Abhishek, Sooryavanshi's blitz 'mind-boggling'
text: Abhishek Sharma- Vaibhav Sooryavanshi India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer was left amazed by the explosive batting of Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after the duo powered India to a record six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third T20I at Wellington's Hnry Stadium on Tuesday. Abhishek 's 113 and Sooryavanshi's 45 set the tone for India's dominant chase, with the opening pair hammering a record 118 runs in the Powerplay, the highest total by any team in the first six overs of a T20 innings. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more The duo added 133 runs for the opening wicket, laying the foundation for India to chase down New Zealand's 199-run target in just 13.2 overs. The victory marked the fastest chase of a target exceeding 190 runs by a Full Member nation and the second-fastest overall, behind Estonia's chase of 192 against Cyprus, which they completed with 42 balls remaining. Iyer admitted that he was left wondering how the openers managed to score so freely after witnessing the conditions for himself when he walked out to bat. "Absolutely stunning. It was pleasing to the eyes the way they played strokes. Also, when Sanju and I went to bat, the ball was seaming, and I was like, how did they manage this? It was simply mind-boggling," Shreyas said after the match. The India captain went on to describe the performance as the best he had witnessed at the international level, particularly given the rate at which the runs came during the Powerplay. "Honestly speaking, getting 100 in 5 overs, I've never seen that before, especially at the international level. And definitely tops it," he added. India's emphatic win gave them an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, underlining their ability to adapt quickly to conditions on New Zealand soil. Iyer stressed the importance of maintaining the same aggressive approach while playing overseas, where unfamiliar conditions and different bowling challenges can test a team's adaptability. "I think it's essential, especially coming overseas (on message for players to keep playing the way they are). You know the conditions are going to be different, and you'll be challenged with a lot of different deliveries. "And just to overcome this by such phenomenal performance, credit where it's due, the way they played today, it was exceptional. And obviously, winning the series with the third match and two more to go, I hope that they keep continuing with the same form and yes, it's just amazing the way the lads pulled up to this occasion. Jet lag at the start and then the way they fitted to the occasion, mind-boggling," he added. While India's batters stole the show, the bowlers also played their part in preventing New Zealand from posting a bigger total. Despite Daryl Mitchell's career-best unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, the hosts finished at 198/3. "So after 10 overs, I realised that anything they were bowling, hard length or even half volleys, it was going into the stands. title: Big shake-up before IPL 2027! Mumbai Indians confirm exits of three coaches, including Lasith Malinga
text: Lasith Malinga (PTI Photo/Kamal Kishore) Mumbai Indians have announced that Lasith Malinga , Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson will leave their roles in the menâs team coaching staff. The franchise thanked the three coaches for their contributions and wished them well for the future. "Mumbai Indians thank Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson for their contributions," Mumbai Indians wrote in a statement. Watch Mumbai Indiansâ new coach Luke Williams on Harmanpreet Kaur, WPL auction and plans for 2027 The franchise also acknowledged their commitment and the relationships they built with the team over the years. "Their commitment, the relationships they have built and the memories they have helped create will always be part of our journey. "We wish each of them the very best in their future endeavours." Contributions of the three coaches Malinga, one of Mumbai Indiansâ most celebrated players, played a major role in the teamâs bowling attack during four IPL title-winning campaigns. He also helped the franchise win the 2011 Champions League T20. After retiring as a player, he returned to MI as a mentor and coach, continuing his long association with the team. Mhambrey first worked with Mumbai Indians from 2010 to 2017 before returning in 2024. The former India bowling coach helped develop the teamâs bowlers and brought valuable experience and knowledge of the franchiseâs working culture. Hopkinson joined Mumbai Indians before the 2025 season after working with the England menâs team. He used his international experience to help improve the teamâs fielding standards. title: 'Both games we could easily have been on the winning side': New Zealand head coach Rob Walter after 2nd T20I defeat to India
text: India's Shreyas Iyer is bowled out by New Zealand's Mitchell Santner during the second T20 cricket international between New Zealand and India in Christchurch, New Zealand. (John Davidson/Photosport via AP) New Zealand head coach Rob Walter believes his team has been competitive in the first two T20Is against India but has failed to make the most of important opportunities. After losing the second match by four wickets, following defeat in the series opener, Walter backed his players to recover and improve in the remaining games. "Both games we could easily have been on the winning side of it, but weren't," Walter said. "Probably missed out on a couple of opportunities each time where you probably would have sealed the game off for us. It's a bit of disappointment but also very happy with how we've played." Watch Nitish Kumar Reddy on Tilak Varma partnership, batting under pressure & all-rounder role Walter said New Zealand had performed well for most of both matches despite limited competitive cricket together before the series. However, mistakes at crucial moments had cost them. Walter praises batting recovery and Santner's bowling New Zealand recovered from losing three wickets during the powerplay in the second T20I to post 180 runs. Walter praised Bevan and Glenn for helping the team reach a competitive total. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines "Even back to last night, three down in the powerplay. It's not often you get to 180 from that position," Walter said. "Bevan and Glen did a hell of a job there to get us to 180 in the end, which was a defendable total if we're honest." He also highlighted captain Mitchell Santner 's four-wicket haul, praising his ability to change pace and control the ball even without much assistance from the pitch. "Sometimes it's unappreciated just how skilful he is. I think last night was a great demonstration of his full repertoire of skill set," Walter said. Walter added that Santner's calm approach and leadership were important strengths for the team. He also admitted that fielding mistakes and a no-ball had hurt New Zealand in the second match. title: Perfect pairing? Why India must stick with Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
text: Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (BCCI Photo) With the T20I series against New Zealand already sealed, the pressure on India to pick the safest XI might have eased. Maybe the team management can focus on a more important question: what should Indiaâs batting order look like two years from now, when the 2028 T20 World Cup is held in Australia and New Zealand? Vaibhav Sooryavanshiâs explosive 45 off 19 balls in the third T20I in Wellington has added to Indiaâs selection headache. Itâs a happy problem. Handed an opportunity after Ishan Kishanâs injury, Sooryavanshi initially struggled at No. 3 in Christchurch as he batted outside the Powerplay. But when India pushed him up to open alongside Abhishek Sharma in Wellington, the 15-year-old was back at his belligerent best. He smashed the first ball to the boundary and never looked back. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more While Abhishekâs century was the headline act, Sooryavanshiâs fearless approach set the tone. The pair raced to a stunning 133-run stand in just seven overs, blowing New Zealand away. The Abhishek-Sooryavanshi partnership also offered a glimpse into the mindset of a new generation of T20 batters, one that sees every ball as a scoring opportunity. The innings also carried a significant subplot. To accommodate Sooryavanshi at the top, Sanju Samson willingly moved down to No. 3 despite enjoying tremendous success as opener. Since returning to the side midway through the T20 World Cup, Samson has formed one of Indiaâs most productive opening partnerships alongside Abhishek. Together, they have scored 1,166 runs in 37 matches and become permanent fixtures at the top of the order. Abhishek was quick to acknowledge the sacrifice. âThe way Sanju bhai batted in the last game, it is not easy to let go of oneâs familiar batting position. That showed his character. Someoneâs going for his position but everyone is selfless and happy for each other, which is the hallmark of a great team,â he said in a BCCI video. The comment revealed an increasingly important characteristic of this Indian side. Unlike previous eras where players were tied to specific positions, this Indian team, under coach Gautam Gambhir , appears willing to embrace flexibility if it benefits the larger cause. That larger cause may now involve finding out just how good a Vaibhav-Abhishek opening pair can become. The youngster himself admitted that batting at No. 3 in Christchurch had forced him away from his natural game. âLast match, I went against my grain as to how I play in T20s. This game, I wanted to give a quick start so that it becomes easy,â Sooryavanshi said. His Wellington knock backed up that assessment. As an opener, there was visible clarity in his approach. He did not have to assess conditions or pace an innings. It was just all out attack. Abhishek, too, felt the impact from the other end. âWhen Vaibhav hit the first ball, he showed aggression. I saw that at the nonstrikerâs end and when you see such a shot, you also feel pumped up. Special mention and credit to Vaibhav for how he played,â Abhishek said. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines The challenge now is fitting everyone into the same side when India are back at full strength. Sooryavanshiâs emergence during IPL 2026 makes it increasingly difficult to keep him on the bench. Yet India already have established performers in Samson and Kishan. However, the debate need not be framed as Vaibhav versus Sanju or Vaibhav versus Kishan. Head coach Gautam Gambhir has repeatedly maintained that only the top two batting positions are fixed and the rest of the order remains flexible. Kishanâs adaptability strengthens that approach. His matchwinning 80 off 46 balls at No. 5 during the Asian Games semifinal vs Sri Lanka showed he can thrive even when he is kept away from the opening slot. It also provided a possible blueprint on how all four batters can feature in the playing XI. With the series result already decided, India can afford to think beyond just the next game. title: Abhishek Sharma scripts history, reaches six-hitting milestone no batter has touched before
text: Abhishek Sharma India opener Abhishek Sharma became the first batter to hit 100 sixes in the powerplay in T20 Internationals during the second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. Abhishek reached the milestone with a six over extra cover off Matt Henry in the third over of India's chase. He had gone past former India captain Rohit Sharma, who hit 98 powerplay sixes in his T20I career, in the series opener on Thursday. Watch Sitanshu Kotak Press Conference: Update on Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav in Playing XI and more Since making his T20I debut in 2024, Abhishek has established himself as one of India's leading six-hitters. title: âWe positioned Travis to be world famousâ: How Travis Kelce built a business empire beyond the NFL with help from two brothers who saw his potential early
text: Travis Kelce built a business empire beyond the NFL with help from two brothers who saw his potential early (Getty Images) Travis Kelce is no longer just the Kansas City Chiefs tight end known for making big plays. He has moved into fashion, business and entertainment, with ventures such as Tru Kolors and Garage Beer adding to his growing profile. But this off-field career did not come together overnight. Andre and Aaron Eanes saw an opportunity in Kelce years before his NFL fame and built a plan to turn his personality into a brand that could reach far beyond football. Their story with Kelce began at the University of Cincinnati. What started as a college friendship eventually became a business partnership that helped shape the tight end's career outside the NFL. How Andre and Aaron Eanes saw a bigger opportunity in Travis Kelce Andre first met Travis Kelce through D.J. Woods, the tight end's college roommate and Andre's childhood friend. The two became close at Cincinnati, where Andre was building an event management business. He helped Kelce and his teammates get into parties and other events. Their connection went beyond the social scene. Andscape reported on November 20, 2023, that Andre and Travis Kelce also worked together at a call centre during the period when Cincinnati suspended the tight end from football in 2010 after a failed drug test. Andre and his twin brother Aaron had launched A&A Management in 2011. They wanted to help athletes build businesses and careers that could last beyond their playing days. Kelce became their second client as he prepared for the 2013 NFL Draft. Aaron had a different idea of what athlete management could look like. In a New York Times profile published on January 2, 2024, he explained, "Agents are contract advisers. I thought instead about a music model and building a business where there's coordination with all their external providers." The brothers wanted to handle more than contract negotiations. They focused on commercials, public appearances, media opportunities and other ways to grow Kelce's name. Their ambition was to make him as recognisable as Dwayne Johnson. Andre explained the thinking in the same New York Times profile: "We positioned Travis to be world famous. We didn't know how it would happen, or when it would happen, or what would help push that further along. But it's always been the thought in the back of our minds." How Travis Kelce took that vision into fashion, beer and  other business The brothers' strategy gave Kelce a platform beyond the football field. His commercial work and television appearances helped introduce him to people who did not necessarily follow the Chiefs. He hosted Saturday Night Live in March 2023 and continued to expand his media presence through the New Heights podcast with Jason Kelce. Aaron also explained why he wanted brands to see Kelce as more than an athlete. In Andscape's November 20, 2023, report, he said, "We had a strategy of we want to maximize national commercials to parlay his characters and his ability to be talent throughout the season so that when people are seeing him, they're seeing him as talent, not as the football player." That thinking fits the business interests Kelce has developed. He founded Tru Kolors, his sportswear and lifestyle brand, in 2019. On August 27, 2025, the label teamed up with American Eagle for a limited-edition collection. Kelce served as creative director and took part in the design process. He also entered the beer business with Jason. On June 12, 2024, the brothers announced they had become significant investors, owners and operators of Garage Beer, an Ohio-based brand. The deal gave them roles in areas such as marketing, sales, distribution and expansion. In the January 2, 2024, New York Times profile, he said, "Actually, it's not that crazy." He added, "It's because it's easy when you have a plan. We're executing that plan." The Eanes brothers did not build Tru Kolors or Garage Beer for him. Instead, they helped create a management strategy that gave him room to pursue opportunities beyond football. title: Former Metropolitan Police employee forged medical certificates to claim around 200 days of sick leave over two years, costing the force nearly Â£19,000 before she admitted fraud in court
text: Image: Canva A former Metropolitan Police employee admitted forging medical certificates to justify around 200 days of absence from work over nearly two years. Natasha Fountain, 29, pleaded guilty to fraud by misrepresentation at Westminster Magistratesâ Court after submitting falsified sick notes to her line manager between November 4, 2022, and May 3, 2024. The scheme cost the Metropolitan Police approximately Â£19,000, according to the court. Fountain had worked as a communications and engagement officer for the force between June 2022 and August 2024. HR Grapevine reported that her initial sickness absence was supported by a genuine medical certificate before she began submitting forged documents. The case underscores the importance of verifying medical documentation and maintaining accurate absence records within public-sector workplaces. Natasha Fountain submitted forged sick notes over nearly two years Fountain, a former communications and engagement officer at the Metropolitan Police, submitted fraudulent medical certificates to justify extended periods away from work. According to HR Grapevine, she worked for the force from June 2022 until August 2024. Although her first sickness absence was supported by a legitimate medical note, she subsequently submitted forged documents between November 4, 2022, and May 3, 2024. These certificates enabled her to claim approximately 200 days of sick leave. Fountain, who appeared at Westminster Magistratesâ Court by video link in March 2026, admitted committing fraud by misrepresentation. Fake medical certificates cost the Metropolitan Police nearly Â£20,000 The fraudulent sick notes resulted in an estimated Â£19,000 cost to the Metropolitan Police, the court heard. Prosecutors raised concerns about the authenticity of the documents, including inconsistencies involving the GP practice that supposedly issued them. There was no record of appointments between Fountain and her GP practice during the relevant dates. The practice had also changed its address, but the correspondence presented by Fountain did not reflect that change. These discrepancies formed part of the evidence surrounding the forged medical certificates. HR Grapevine reported that the documents had been used to justify her prolonged absence from the force. Court hears former Met employee had physical and mental health difficulties The court also heard that Fountain had experienced physical and mental health difficulties, including severe anxiety. Her condition reportedly prevented her from returning to her GP to obtain ongoing treatment and genuine medical certificates. District Judge Briony Clarke described the fraud as "quite sophisticated", explaining that Fountain had gone beyond simply lying by actively forging documents. The judge said further information was needed about Fountain's health during the period in question. She indicated that the court should examine whether genuine medical conditions had affected her ability to work, rather than considering the fraud without that context. Natasha Fountain admitted fraud and awaits sentencing Fountain pleaded guilty to fraud by misrepresentation at Westminster Magistratesâ Court in March 2026. District Judge Briony Clarke delayed sentencing to allow further information about her health at the time of the offences to be gathered. The judge said that any genuine medical conditions affecting her ability to work could be relevant to the sentencing decision. Fountain was granted unconditional bail and was due to return to Westminster Magistratesâ Court on April 20, 2026, for sentencing, according to HR Grapevine's March 26 report. title: IPL 2027: Amidst winds of change, Rohit Sharma is the glue Mumbai Indians need right now
text: Rohit Sharma and Kieron Pollard NEW DELHI: Kieron Pollard 's elevation as the new head coach and the exits of Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson from the Mumbai Indians (MI) setup have already pressed the reset button in the camp. Appointments for the fielding coach and assistant coach are still pending, but the winds of change have well and truly arrived as the five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) winners look to return to their glory days. The biggest, and most crucial, piece in the puzzle, however, remains captaincy. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more Should they go back to Rohit Sharma ? The man who led them to five titles and understands the setup better than any other player? Or should they adopt a forward-looking approach with someone like Tilak Varma ? What about Jasprit Bumrah and Suryakumar Yadav? Rohit is 39 and isn't the best bet the franchise can make for the next cycle, but it's more about restoring normalcy, allowing Pollard to ease into his new role and possibly grooming the next leader in the final year of the ongoing cycle. After sweeping changes to the support staff, a sense of familiarity in the leadership group will only make the transition and preparation for future challenges smoother. Pollard and Rohit played together for several years at MI. The West Indian was part of the famous "engine room", also featuring Hardik and Krunal Pandya, that drove the franchise forward during their golden days and flourished when Rohit was at the helm. This is not to suggest that the two are the perfect recipe to restore order in that dressing room, but looking towards an inexperienced candidate at this stage will only complicate matters further. Tilak is taking giant strides in his cricketing career and is certainly the future leader of MI and Indian cricket. But right now, it's the delicate balancing act between need and want that could help the management find some answers. title: Drama! Qais Ahmed's injury moment brings back memories of Gulbadin Naib's T20 World Cup incident
text: Qais Ahmed and Gulbadin Naib (Image credit: Agencies) NEW DELHI: Qais Ahmed grabbed attention in the closing stages of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. The Afghanistan batter's injury moment reminded fans of Gulbadin Naib's incident during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan put up a determined batting effort to secure a draw at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium. The hosts batted for 142 overs to avoid defeat against their Asian rivals. Qais played an important role in ensuring that the efforts of Afghanistan's batters, especially Sediqullah Atal, did not go in vain. Batting at number nine, he remained unbeaten on 49 off 80 balls and helped his team survive the final stages of the match. Watch Tilak Varma on India's aggressive approach & his middle-order role Qais Ahmed's injury moment in the final overs With just 10 minutes left in the match, Qais blocked a delivery from Taijul Islam in the third-last over before going down while holding his left hamstring. The moment caught the attention of social media users, while Bangladesh players appeared pleased with the situation. The incident reminded fans of Naib's injury moment against Bangladesh during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan won that match to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time. Qais made another important contribution in the final over, hitting two sixes as Afghanistan and Bangladesh settled for a draw. Sediqullah Atal scores maiden Test century Atal played a key role in Afghanistan's effort to save the Test. He scored 111 off 333 balls to register the first Test century of his career. He also became the first Afghanistan batter to score a century in the fourth innings of a Test match. Captain Rahmat Shah also had a memorable game. In his first Test as captain, he scored 105 in the first innings and followed it up with 51 in the second. Rahmat became only the sixth male cricketer to score a century and a half-century on his Test captaincy debut. Gulbadin Naib's injury incident at T20 World Cup 2024 Afghanistan created history at the 2024 T20 World Cup by beating Bangladesh to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time. However, the match also drew attention because of an incident involving Naib. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines During the 12th over of Bangladesh's innings, Naib went down holding his hamstring shortly after head coach Jonathan Trott was seen signalling to the players to slow the game down. At that stage, Afghanistan were two runs ahead under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, with the match finely balanced. Naib's injury led to the physios coming onto the field. Play was then stopped as rain interrupted the match. When the teams returned after a short break, Naib appeared to be moving comfortably. This led to criticism from some fans and experts, who questioned the timing of the incident and suggested it may have helped Afghanistan. Afghanistan eventually defeated Najmul Hossain Shanto's Bangladesh by eight runs under the DLS method. The result also knocked Australia out of the race for a semi-final spot.
