title: 72% of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh political parties fail to disclose finances: Association for Democratic Reforms
text: 72% of T, AP political parties fail to disclose finances: ADR Hyderabad : Nearly three-fourths of registered unrecognised political parties in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh failed to publicly disclose either their annual audit statements or contribution reports for 2024-25, raising fresh concerns over transparency and financial accountability in the political system, according to a report released by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) on Thursday. The report also highlighted discrepancies in donation disclosures made by two Telangana-based parties. Of the 169 registered unrecognised political parties (RUPPs) in the two states, 123, or 72%, had neither annual audit statements nor contribution reports available on the websites of the respective chief electoral officers. 31 parties have both statements online Telangana accounted for 78 of the 123 parties without either disclosure, representing 75% of its 104 RUPPs. In Andhra Pradesh, 45 of the 65 such parties had not made either report available. Only 31 parties across both states had uploaded both the audit statement and contribution report. Telangana accounted for 17 of these parties, while Andhra Pradesh had 14. Another 15 parties had only one of the two disclosures available. In Telangana, six parties had uploaded only audit statements and three only contribution reports. In Andhra Pradesh, two parties had only audit statements available, while four had uploaded only contribution reports. Donation figures differ The ADR report also flagged inconsistencies in the financial disclosures of two Telangana-based parties. A Hyderabad-based political party reported zero income and zero total donations for 2024-25, but disclosed receiving â¹1.29 lakh in contributions above â¹20,000. The party reported expenditure of â¹300 during the year. It had contested seven seats in the 2023 Telangana assembly elections, polling 49,423 votes without winning any seat. Similarly, Vishwa Bharath Party, registered in Dec 2021, declared an income of â¹900, total donations of â¹200 and expenditure of â¹5,000. However, its contribution report showed donations exceeding â¹20,000 amounting to â¹30,000. The party contested one assembly constituency in the 2023 elections, securing 55 votes. The two Telangana parties were among 14 parties across the country whose reported contributions above â¹20,000 exceeded their declared total donations. ADR noted that the reasons for such discrepancies can be established only after examining the partiesâ original accounts and contribution reports. The report also noted that the Andhra Pradesh CEOâs website did not provide consolidated information on the submission status of annual reports for 2024-25. In contrast, Telanganaâs CEO website carried details on the status of audit report submissions by political parties. Available disclosures showed that Telangana-based parties reported a combined income of â¹18.9 lakh and expenditure of â¹15.8 lakh. Parties in Andhra Pradesh reported income of â¹70.8 lakh and expenditure of â¹78.2 lakh. Together, the parties declared total donations of â¹82.7 lakh, while contributions exceeding â¹20,000 amounted to nearly â¹1.9 crore. Nationally, ADR examined financial disclosures of 2,074 registered unrecognised political parties, of which only 461 had both audit statements and contribution reports available. title: 'Most inexperienced bowling attack': Gautam Gambhir flags India's biggest challenge ahead of New Zealand ODIs
text: India's head coach Gautam Gambhir with Arshdeep Singh. (PTI Photo) NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has identified the inexperienced bowling attack as the biggest challenge facing the visitors in the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4. With Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya unavailable, India will have to depend on a relatively inexperienced group of pacers, led by Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh . Gambhir believes that if India manage to deliver results in the ODI series, the bowlers should receive much of the credit rather than the more experienced batting unit. The challenge is particularly significant with India having to balance preparations for the white-ball matches and the two-Test series scheduled towards the end of the tour. Watch Gautam Gambhir on India's challenges, young players & ODI series "It's important for me to win every series. It's not just about winning in New Zealand. It's challenging to win every series. Because if you look at it, this will probably be the most inexperienced bowling attack in ODI cricket," Gambhir said on Sunday. The numbers underline his concern. Siraj, with 51 ODIs, is the most experienced pacer in the group. Arshdeep has played 18, while Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj have one ODI each. Gurnoor Brar has featured in nine. "No one will talk about it. But if you look at it, Aqib Nabi (1 ODI). Anshul Khamboj, one match. Gurnoor, how many? 10 matches (nine). Only Arshdeep is our most experienced bowler (18). "Despite that, if we do well in the one-day series, the credit will go to this bowling attack. It will go to these boys. We have experience in batting. We have a lot of experience in batting. "But when you come overseas, your bowlers win the series, especially in one-day and Test cricket. So if we go ahead and do well in one-day cricket, a lot of credit should be given to these bowlers rather than talking too much about the batters," he added. Gambhir's challenge to Abhishek Sharma Gambhir also spoke about the improvement Abhishek Sharma showed against New Zealand off-spinner Michael Bracewell during the five-match T20I series. The India opener had struggled against off-spin earlier in the series but worked on that aspect of his batting during extended net sessions with the head coach, himself a former accomplished player of spin bowling. "Obviously, Abhishek has struggled a bit with off-spin. The more he gets better at it, obviously, he will become an overall better player. And you want to keep improving yourself because the opposition keeps studying you. "The way you bat, the way you make runs, the speed with which you bat. So if you improve your game, the different areas, if you improve against different bowlers, you will be one step ahead of the opposition. "So that's what I was talking about. Because in the first match, when he was bowling off-spin, obviously, he got a little tied up. It was just a very tactical and technical stuff that we spoke about," Gambhir said. Gambhir hails India's 'incredible' T20I series win The coach also reflected on India's 3-2 T20I series victory, praising the team's ability to overcome limited preparation time and unfamiliar conditions. India had only one training session after arriving in New Zealand before the October 22 opener in Christchurch, but won the first three matches to seal the series. The hosts claimed the final two games. "Look, first of all, obviously it's an incredible effort because the boys got only one day to prepare," Gambhir said after the fifth and final T20I. "They arrived on the 20th (of October), we practiced on the 21st... different conditions, different weather conditions, different dimensions, playing against a quality side like New Zealand in their own backyard with the amount of experience they had in T20 cricket, plus most of the boys were touring New Zealand for the first time. "Boys can be extremely proud of their efforts, especially when you hardly got any time to prepare." title: âKhelunga bhi waise hiâ: Abhishek Sharma reveals Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's âBhaag Milkha Bhaagâ message before NZ blitz
text: India's Abhishek Sharma, left, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP/PTI) India opener Abhishek Sharma revealed that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had promised to bat fearlessly, borrowing an iconic dialogue from the Bollywood film Bhaag Milkha Bhaag , during a net session before the third T20I against New Zealand. The 15-year-old then delivered on his words with an explosive innings that helped India seal the series. Sooryavanshi told Abhishek he would play in the same manner as the character in the film, using the dialogue, âBhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hiâ, which translates to âBrother, I will play the same wayâ. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more The young left-hander lived up to his promise, smashing 45 off just 19 balls to give India a flying start in their chase of 199. Opening alongside Sooryavanshi, Abhishek went on to blast 113 off 38 deliveries as India cruised to a six-wicket victory in just 13.2 overs at the Hnry Stadium on Tuesday. Speaking in a video shared by the BCCI after the match, Abhishek recalled the conversation and credited Sooryavanshi's aggressive start with helping set the tone for the chase. âYesterday, Vaibhav told me something in the nets that I will play the same way as in the Milkha Singh movie Bhag Milkha Bhag dialogue âBhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hiâ,â Abhishek said. The India opener explained that Sooryavanshi's intent was particularly significant against New Zealand's frontline fast bowler. Watching from the non-striker's end, Abhishek said the teenager's aggression immediately lifted his confidence. âWhen you are chasing 200 or 190, his first ball, first over, is his main fast baller. And if you show such aggression as an opener. Because I was on the other side, so I saw that. On the first ball, the non-striker gets excited,â he said. Abhishek was quick to acknowledge the youngster's contribution to the result, stressing that the opening partnership played a crucial role in India's successful chase. âI feel special mention to Vaibhav. What he did today, I think, played a very crucial role today. So it goes to him,â he added. India also reached 50 in just 2.2 overs, equalling the joint-fastest team fifty in the format, before crossing the 100-run mark inside five overs. title: Man gets two years of rigorous imprisonment for showing obscene films to minors
text: Thiruvananthapuram: A fast-track court in Attingal sentenced a 45-year-old man to two years of rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 for showing obscene films to two minor girls. Judge C R Bijukumar, who pronounced the verdict, said that in default of payment of the fine, the accused would have to undergo an additional two months of rigorous imprisonment. Attingal fast-track court found Benny Thankachan, a native of Edamulakkal in Kollam, guilty under Section 354A(2) read with Section 354A(1)(iii) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 12 read with Section 11(iii) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on June 19, 2024. The accused had allegedly shown sexually explicit films to the two girls, both aged 12. Kilimanoor Police registered a case on June 20, 2024, and launched an investigation. The investigation was conducted by sub-inspector R Rajikrishna, who subsequently filed the chargesheet before the court. During the trial, the prosecution examined 22 witnesses and produced 25 documents as evidence. The court also ordered that, if the fine amount is recovered, Rs 25,000 each be paid to the two survivors as compensation. It further recommended compensation for them through the district legal services authority, Thiruvananthapuram. title: Chips are down
text: Representative image The pause might be temporary, but markets did well to reassess their AI play in Oct Secretly, many of us want AI to go away like a bad dream. We have no stomach for those noisy, thirsty and hungry data centres, âchipflationâ, AI slop, and job losses. But AI is here to stay. That much is certain. What might happen â and looks probable after a sobering Oct â is that some of the market enthusiasm for AI might cool. We know a âbustâ would be music to many ears, and if markets were rational it would have happened two years ago. For now, though, it looks like markets have turned sceptical. So Apple, which has the least AI exposure among Big Tech, is back to being the worldâs most valuable company, ahead of chipmaker Nvidia. Yes, this Apple-Nvidia switch happened in July too, and sceptics might be reading too much into it this time, but there are other signs. Like Nasdaqâs $2tn wipeout during the month. Or Alphabetâs 12% share price drop on Thursday, S&P Globalâs negative outlook for Meta Platforms, and reports of OpenAI reducing its funding target by $10bn in the latest round. And while we werenât paying attention, Oct had started with data centre firm Firmus shelving its IPO in Australia after institutional investors didnât show interest. Suddenly, AI euphoria seems missing. It might not be a case of cold feet yet, but anxiety is palpable among investors. Unlike 2024, when US Fed cut interest rates thrice, and Nvidia overtook Apple for the first time, 2026 is ending with the Fed in a hawkish mood. AI firms are increasingly raising money via new shares and bonds. Old investors hate new shares because they weaken prospects of future per-share earnings, while debt has to be repaid at all costs, and itâs growing costlier. With AI investments approaching $1tn this year, the debt albatross is massive anyway. What if, investors are asking, a Chinese open-source model comes along and undercuts the US-centric AI business. It could drive down valuations sharply. And that would have serious consequences for the global economy, because anywhere from 20% to 30% of US GDP growth today is AI-led. The Big Seven account for 35% of S&P 500. A sudden slowdown in US wonât spare anyone, because US is the biggest market. For IMF, an AI asset price crash is among the top threats to the global economy right now. So if markets are looking wary, belatedly, thatâs not bad. Weâll know their pulse better after Anthropicâs upcoming IPO. Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

title: Cash instead of foodgrains: State approves DBT for APL farmers in 14 districts
text: A standard operating procedure (SOP) for the scheme has also been laid out by state govt Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: The state govt has approved the onboarding of the direct benefit transfer (DBT) scheme for above poverty line (APL) saffron ration card-holding farmers in 14 farmer suicide-hit districts on the MahaDBT 2.0 portal. It has also laid down a standard operating procedure (SOP) for the scheme. Under the scheme, the benefit amount will be transferred to the Aadhaar-linked bank account of the woman head of the household. If there is no woman head, or if her account is not Aadhaar-linked, the amount will be credited to the account of a senior male member or another member of the family. The Aadhaar numbers of all members listed on the ration card must be linked to the Ration Card Management System (RCMS), and e-KYC of every beneficiary is mandatory. Tehsil offices will guide members who do not have Aadhaar cards on the process of obtaining them. The govt resolution (GR), issued by the food, civil supplies and consumer protection department on Oct 30, covers Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Nanded, Beed, Dharashiv, Parbhani, Latur, Hingoli, Amravati, Washim, Akola, Buldhana, Yavatmal, and Wardha. According to the GR, eligible farmers not covered under the National Food Security Act, 2013, will receive Rs 170 per beneficiary per month in cash instead of foodgrains. The scheme was re-engineered under govt process re-engineering and onboarded on MahaDBT 2.0 (mahadbt2.maharashtra.gov.in) to make it more transparent, faster, error-free and integrated. A department secretary-led review meeting on Jan 22-23, 2025, decided to route the scheme through MahaIT-run direct benefit transfer. Approved through a Feb 28, 2023, GR, it provided Rs 150 monthly from Jan 2023. A June 20, 2024, circular raised this to Rs 170 from April 2024. The GR also referred to an earlier GR dated July 24, 2015. The GR states that âthe amount will be revised every year in line with hikes in the minimum support price, as per the Cash Transfer of Food Subsidy Rules, 2015, notified by the Centre. The revised sum will be rounded off to the next multiple of Rs 10â. Under the SOP, data of eligible ration card holders on the Ration Card Management System (RCMS) will be given to Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Ltd. It will then flow automatically to MahaDBT 2.0 through the Mahasarathi system. Officials at taluka, district and state levels will get logins. Taluka-level officers will check RCMS data month-wise, financial year-wise and fair price shop-wise. They will select an eligible member with an Aadhaar-linked bank account, preferably the woman head of the family, and forward the application to the district. If she has no such account, another member's Aadhaar-linked account will be chosen. District-level officers (DSO) will scrutinise the applications and either give bulk approval or reject them with reasons if defects are found. The state nodal officer (SNO) will complete the âallocate beneficiariesâ process after checking the number of approved beneficiaries by financial year and instalment, and the admissible funds. The SNO will then generate a bill or Request for Transfer (RFT) and submit it to the drawing and disbursing officer (DDO). The DDO will digitally sign the RFT, generate and digitally sign an XML file and trigger payment. Rs 170 per member per month will then be credited to Aadhaar-linked accounts. The benefit is to be disbursed through MahaDBT 2.0 from April 2026. New ration card holders will become eligible from the month after their RCMS registration is completed. title: CBI adds charges carrying life term in bank recruitment racket probe
text: Mumbai: CBI has invoked stringent charges of forgery of valuable security and provisions of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in its probe into an alleged impersonation racket involving 135 candidates selected through Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) recruitment examinations. The forgery charge attracts a maximum punishment of life imprisonment. A special court on Friday took on record CBIâs intimation to invoke additional penal provisions. It is alleged that at least 180 such aspirants cleared and are employed in various banks. Sections 3, 4 and 5 are offences of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act that are related to prohibition of unfair means, disruption and criminal conspiracy. When invoked with the penal provisions, Section 10 prescribes imprisonment of up to five years and a Rs 10 lakh fine for individual offenders, while Section 11 is related to organised crime syndicates with a harsher maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 1 crore. âHaving considered the submissions and the record, it appears that based upon the facts revealed during the course of investigation, the provisions as aforementioned are invokedâ¦,â the judge said. The case was registered on Aug 20, 2026, on the complaint of the Head, Research and Development, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, Mumbai. The FIR was lodged against Ashish Avinash and 134 others for alleged fraudulent selection through impersonation for appointments to different posts in various banks in examinations conducted by IBPS between 2020 and 2024. According to CBI, field verification of the biometrics of suspected impersonators during the investigation revealed that accused Rajeev Ranjan , Vishwa Bhaskar, Abhishek Kumar alias Roshan and Manish Kumar had allegedly appeared in place of the actual candidates at different stages of the recruitment process. The agency also examined invigilators Sagar Gupta and Sakshi Chhipa, who were posted at examination centres in Lucknow and Ajmer, Rajasthan, respectively. CBI told the court that the impersonators had allegedly signed and provided sample handwriting on admit cards in the names of the original candidates in the presence of the invigilators. On this basis, the investigating officer sought to invoke Section 467 of the IPC, which deals with forgery of valuable security, will or authority to make or transfer valuable security. The agency further submitted that the respondent candidate arrayed as accused No 129 had allegedly secured a job after one Sonu Kumar appeared in his place on Aug 30, 2024, and Sept 29, 2024. On account of this allegation, CBI sought to invoke Sections 3, 4 and 5 read with Sections 10 and 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. title: Harmanpreet Kaur breaks down  on live TV after sensational 91, reveals what has changed
text: Harmanpreet Kaur (Screengrab) Harmanpreet Kaur struggled to hold back her emotions after producing a stunning comeback with the bat, smashing an unbeaten 91 off just 41 balls against Zimbabwe in the third and final T20I. The former India captain's emotional moment came during an innings-break interview, when she reflected on her return to form and thanked those who had backed her through a difficult period. The 37-year-old, who stepped down as India's captain across formats earlier this month, had gone 10 matches without a half-century. Her struggles with the bat had continued through the Women's T20 Asia Cup and the Asian Games, even as India went on to win both tournaments comfortably. But against Zimbabwe, Harmanpreet looked a different batter, finding her rhythm and striking the ball with authority. Her unbeaten knock featured 10 fours and five sixes, with several powerful hits down the ground. As she spoke to the host broadcaster at the break, the 37-year-old became emotional and struggled to hold back her tears. "It feels great. Just wanted to enjoy myself, and great that I got some time in the middle and really enjoyed myself on the field," she said. During the conversation, Harmanpreet also acknowledged former India women's team head coach WV Raman, who was part of the broadcast, for his words of encouragement. "I just wanted to bat as long as possible, and glad that I was able to do that. I think I should give credit to you also (to WV Raman). "The moment we came, you stepped in and you said, 'Now you do what you want to do,' and that's what I want to do, and really want to enjoy myself. Thanks for those words." Harmanpreet said stepping down as captain had eased the pressure on her, allowing her to focus on enjoying her time in the middle. "I don't think there is any pressure anymore. Now it's all about going out there and enjoying myself on the field, and that's exactly what I want to do," she said. She also credited the time spent working in the nets after the Asian Games, thanking batting coach Himanshu Chawla for helping her prepare for the innings. "After the Asian Games, I got some time in the nets. I really want to thank Himanshu bhaiya, who's been working really hard on me, and today's batting was all him." The knock marked Harmanpreet's first half-century since beginning her stint as a non-captain. Her unbeaten 91 was also the second-highest individual score by an Indian batter at No. 4 or lower in Women's T20Is, behind her own 103 against New Zealand at Providence during the 2018 T20 World Cup. title: 'There is pressure on us': Pakistan's ICC trophy drought adds to players' burden
text: Fakhar Zaman (Image credit: AFP) Experienced top-order batter Fakhar Zaman believes Pakistan can end their wait for an ICC trophy at next year's 50-overs World Cup, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Speaking to the media in Rawalpindi on Saturday, Fakhar said Pakistan's players had held detailed discussions about their failure to win an ICC title since 2017. Watch Bombay Sport Exchange: Jonty Rhodes on why Indian parents must rethink sport âThere is pressure on us as a team to deliver an ICC trophy, and we have had extensive discussions about ending the country's wait for a major international trophy,â he said, as quoted by news agency PTI. Pakistan last reached the final of an ICC tournament at the 2022 T20 World Cup in Australia, where they lost to England in Melbourne. Fakhar acknowledged that the team's failure to win an ICC title had disappointed fans, while pointing out that strong performances brought appreciation from the public. âIt is natural (that) people are disappointed about Pakistan not being able to win an ICC title for long, and we also know that when we do well, we are showered with love and admiration,â Fakhar said. âWhen you perform well, people show you more love. When you do not perform well, naturally, they are disappointed. Whether senior or junior, every player tries to perform to the best of their ability and improve in their profession.â He added that winning a trophy brought a different kind of happiness compared to reaching the latter stages of a tournament. âThe happiness you experience as a nation after winning a trophy is different from reaching semi-finals or finals,â he added. Fakhar said the players were serious about ending Pakistan's wait for an ICC title and hoped to bring the World Cup trophy home. âWe are taking it very seriously. We will do our best, and we hope Allah helps us bring the World Cup trophy back to Pakistan,â he said. The upcoming tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka will be an important part of Pakistan's preparations, with the team looking to settle on the right combination for next year's ODI World Cup. âThe idea is to start building a perfect combination for the World Cup from now, and the good thing is most of our players are going into the tri-series having played domestic cricket,â Fakhar said. He also highlighted the value of playing domestic 50-overs cricket before taking on international opposition in the format. âWhen you play 50-overs cricket after First-Class, it is much easier to adapt, but going from T20 to ODIs is never easy. It is encouraging that all the players have come through the season and are in very good touch,â he added. title: 99 runs leaked in 2 T20Is! Bhuvneshwar Kumar gets a message from Morne Morkel
text: Bhuvneshwar Kumar (BCCI Photo) India bowling coach Morne Morkel has asked Bhuvneshwar Kumar to stay calm, ignore outside pressure and focus on his own game as the experienced fast bowler tries to find his rhythm after returning to the T20I team following a four-year gap. Bhuvneshwar's comeback has not gone as planned. The 36-year-old conceded 49 runs in the first T20I against New Zealand and 50 in the second, taking just one wicket across the two matches. His economy rate of 12.37 has been the highest among India's bowlers in the series. Watch Nitish Kumar Reddy on Tilak Varma partnership, batting under pressure & all-rounder role With India leading 2-0 in the five-match series, Morkel has backed the veteran pacer to improve as he gets more opportunities on the field. 'Block the expectation factor out' Morkel said Bhuvneshwar would naturally face expectations after returning to the international stage following four years away from the T20I side. He also pointed to the bowler's strong performances in the IPL. "I've got a lot of sympathy for his return. There will be expectations after four years to come back. He has done exceptionally well in the IPL and bowled really well," Morkel said on the eve of the third T20I. The bowling coach said preparing for international cricket was not easy, especially when a player had limited time to get ready before the series. "One challenge is to block the expectation factor out. Two, leading into selection, he trained for a month, but playing international cricket is a different beast where the margins are small. title: Powering fourth: Karnataka moves up in Indiaâs TOEFL league, leapfrogs Gujarat
text: Karnataka overtakes Gujarat, with 9.3% share of Indiaâs test-takers in FY 2025-26 Bengaluru: Karnataka has overtaken Gujarat to become the fourth-largest state in terms of TOEFL-takers, according to data shared by Educational Testing Service (ETS), which administers the English-language test. The stateâs share of test-takers has seen a consistent increase, up from 8.1% in FY 2023-24 to 8.7% in FY 2024-25 and 9.3% in FY 2025-26. Telangana leads overall with a share of 18.1%, followed by Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh (15.1% each). Karnataka is marginally ahead of Gujarat at 9%. âBengaluru continues to be a significant centre for TOEFL participation. The city ranked fourth among Indiaâs leading TOEFL iBT test-taking cities in 2021 before moving to third place in 2022 and 2023. Mysuru also featured among the countryâs top 10 test-taking cities in 2023,â said Karan Lalit, executive director â South Asia, TOEFL & GRE, ETS. According to ETS, it currently has more than 60 active institutional partners across Karnataka, including Bengaluru, Mangaluru, Mysuru, Hubballi and Dharwad. These partnerships support student outreach, awareness initiatives and access to TOEFL preparation resources. However, access to testing infrastructure remains concentrated in Bengaluru, which has four TOEFL test centres. ETS said it is in discussions with several universities and colleges across Karnataka to strengthen student support, particularly in test preparation and registration. While the US, UK, Canada and Australia continue to be popular choices among Indian students, interest in destinations such as Germany, France, Ireland and countries in the Middle East is also growing. âAt a global level, TOEFL score reports sent to universities in Japan increased by 10% in FY 2025-26, while reports sent to universities in Hong Kong increased by 24% in 2025. These figures reflect global ETS data and should not be interpreted as trends specific to Karnataka,â Lalit said. ETS said students are increasingly evaluating multiple countries before making study-abroad decisions, taking into account visa regulations, affordability, admission requirements, and post-study work opportunities. âGermany enrolled approximately 59,000 Indian students in the 2024-25 winter semester, representing a year-on-year growth of around 20%. France recorded approximately 9,100 Indian students in 2025. Ireland recorded 9,175 Indian students in 2024-25. The Niti Aayog report on internationalisation of higher education also identifies the UAE as a destination for Indian students. These figures illustrate the range of international education markets attracting Indian students,â he said. TOEFL iBT is accepted by more than 13,500 institutions across over 160 countries as a common English-language proficiency assessment when applying to universities in different destinations. title: 'Ka mau te wehi': Shreyas Iyer's four-word post after India win NZ series leaves fans searching for meaning
text: Shreyas Iyer (Pic credit: Iyer's X post) NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer had a message for his team and fans after guiding the side to a 3-2 T20I series victory over New Zealand, but it was not in English or Hindi. Instead, Iyer chose a four-word Maori expression that left many cricket fans curious about its meaning. Taking to social media after the series concluded on Sunday, Iyer shared a set of photographs from India's campaign, accompanied by the caption "Ka mau te wehi" and a trophy emoji. The unusual phrase quickly caught attention, with fans and cricket followers trying to decipher what the India skipper was attempting to convey through his post. Watch Inside Gill and KL Rahul's intense training | Why no Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma | Nets footage As it turned out, Iyer had picked a popular Maori expression native to New Zealand, the country where India had just completed their international assignment. The phrase, pronounced approximately kah mow teh feh-hee, is an enthusiastic expression of admiration and excitement. It translates to "Awesome!", "That's amazing!" or "Absolutely brilliant!" in everyday usage. What does 'Ka mau te wehi' mean? "Ka mau te wehi" is a Maori kiwaha (colloquial saying or idiom) used to express admiration, amazement or appreciation for something exceptional. While its literal sense is associated with being gripped by awe or wonder, its everyday meaning is closer to saying "Fantastic!", "Outstanding!" or "What a performance!" The word wehi conveys a sense of awe, wonder or an intense emotional reaction. In Maori cultural and performing arts traditions, including kapa haka, it can describe the powerful feeling of being moved or impressed by a performance. Iyer's choice of words was particularly fitting for an Indian side that had managed to secure a series victory on New Zealand soil despite a challenging finish. India had taken an unassailable 3-0 lead by winning the first three matches, but New Zealand fought back with victories in the final two games. What Shreyas Iyer said after India's series win Despite the series triumph, Iyer admitted that India could have performed better, particularly after failing to capitalise on a promising batting platform in the final T20I. Reflecting on the seven-wicket defeat, the India captain pointed to the middle-order collapse after his partnership with Ishan Kishan had provided momentum. "It was plausible honestly. We could have been better considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I, we created the momentum. And then from there on we lost back-to-back wickets. And then suddenly pressure on the new batsman," Iyer said during the post-match presentation. title: Mumbai loses 18.9 sq km of mangroves in 18 years, fish nurseries under pressure: Study
text: Mangroves Mumbai: Mumbai has lost nearly a fifth of its mangrove cover in 18 years, raising concerns over the survival of natural fish nurseries that sustain coastal biodiversity and support fishing communities. Between 2006 and 2024, mangrove cover along the cityâs coastline declined 17.41%, with researchers mapping 30.20 sq km of mangroves lost against just 11.32 sq km of new growth. These are the findings of a study published online on Oct 26 that highlight the growing ecological vulnerability of Mumbaiâs coastal landscape. The loss is significant not merely because the city is losing its green buffers, but because mangroves perform an important, less visible function: their intricate root systems provide shelter, food and nursery habitats for juvenile fish, prawns, crabs and other aquatic organisms. The study published in Elsevier journal Total Environment Advances by Vinod Kumar Yadav and Durgesh Kumar Jha assessed four coastal sectors â Versova-Madh Island-Malad (VMM), Gorai Creek, Thane Creek and Sewri-Chembur-Trombay â using satellite images from 2006, 2012, 2018 and 2024. The researchers found that mapped mangrove area declined from 75.07 sq km in 2006 to 61.99 sq km in 2024. Their common-resolution transition analysis recorded 30.20 sq km of loss and 11.32 sq km of gain, resulting in a net reduction of 18.89 sq km. The largest net decline occurred between 2012 and 2018. The composition of the surviving vegetation has also changed. Open mangrove cover declined 76.8% and sparse mangrove cover by 19.28%, indicating substantial changes in the density and structure of the ecosystem. This matters because the ecological functions of a mangrove forest depend not just on its geographical spread but also on its health, density and continuity. For fisheries scientists, this raises an important question: how much of the loss and degradation of mangrove habitats is affecting the availability of breeding and nursery grounds for fish and shellfish in Mumbaiâs creeks? A decline in suitable juvenile habitats can potentially affect recruitment into adult fish populations, although the extent of any impact on fish stocks or fishing yields would need to be established through independent fisheries surveys. The study itself does not measure fish populations, species diversity or fishing catches. Its contribution is to establish the scale and geographical pattern of mangrove change, providing a scientific basis for further investigation into its consequences for aquatic biodiversity and fisheries. The researchers used four machine-learning methods â Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Trees and Support Vector Machine â to classify satellite imagery and map changes in mangrove cover. They also examined the effect of differences in satellite resolution. Between 2018 and 2024, the estimated decline was 5.03% at the native 10-metre resolution of Sentinel-2 imagery and 6.75% after aggregation to a common 30-metre resolution. Despite the difference in estimates, both analyses indicated a continuing decline. The implications extend to the cityâs protection against climate-related risks. Mangroves stabilise shorelines, trap sediments, help regulate nutrient cycles and reduce the force of waves and storm surges. Their degradation can leave coastal stretches more vulnerable to erosion and flooding, particularly as Mumbai faces increasingly intense rainfall and rising coastal risks. The findings also call for a closer examination of restoration efforts. title: CAG Flags NMCâs Rs1,646cr Pending Utilisation Certificates, Negative Balance In Smart City Account
text: CAG Audit Nagpur: A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) inspection audit of Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has flagged several financial and accounting lapses, including pending utilisation certificates (UCs) worth Rs1,646 crore, unadjusted advances of Rs4.2 crore and a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the Nagpur Smart and Sustainable City Development Corporation Ltd account (NSSCDCL). The audit observations raise questions about the civic bodyâs financial management, monitoring of govt grants and internal accounting controls. The findings are part of the inspection report on the accounts of NMCâs chief accounts and finance officer for the period covered by the audit. One of the major concerns is the non-submission of utilisation certificates worth Rs1,646 crore. The pending certificates relate to grants received from govt agencies and are required to establish that funds were spent for their sanctioned purposes. The delay could complicate financial accountability and affect the processing of future grants. The audit also highlights a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the account of NSSCDCL. The provisional balance sheet for 2024-25 showed the deficit under grants and contributions for specific purposes. The report also recorded a reduction in the grant balance for special city development projects. Another observation concerns advances of Rs4.20 crore paid to various officials and department heads that remain unadjusted. The audit sought details of pending advances, indicating shortcomings in monitoring and reconciliation of expenditure. The report also raised concerns over statutory accounting procedures. While NMCâs annual accounts for 2023-24 were examined and approved by the chief auditor, the accounts for 2024-25 had been prepared but further action was still underway. The audit sought an update on compliance with statutory requirements. Among other outstanding observations are a loan liability of Rs94.41 crore pending for over 16 years and avoidable interest payments linked to delays in loan-related procedures. Former NCP corporator Vedprakash Arya submitted a memorandum to municipal commissioner Vipin Itankar, demanding a high-level inquiry into the financial irregularities and accountability of officials concerned. title: Tech glitches hit A to B khata upgrade
text: Bengaluru: Thousands of property owners waiting to upgrade from B-khata to A-khata within Greater Bengaluru Authority limits are stuck, with portal glitches and faulty document uploads holding up their applications for more than 10 days now. Without A-khata, owners struggle to access civic services, complete property transactions or get bank loans. Many said sales and registrations had stalled, while some claimed their applications were rejected despite repeated online attempts. Thereâs no clear indication of how soon the system will be restored, sources said. The delay follows the Sept 22 launch of upgraded e-Aasthi 2.0 software, meant to simplify khata services, cut paperwork and reduce visits to govt offices. Citizens soon complained of trouble uploading documents. GBA officials said minor glitches in the early days had been fixed and maintained there were no major problems with the software, but complaints continued. Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda told TOI officials found some owners had uploaded blank files, wrong property photographs or incorrect locations. âIâve instructed officials to hold special adalats and clear pending applications soon,â he added. Then deputy CM DK Shivakumar had announced the Namma Khate Namma Hakku campaign, with a 100-day window that ended on Aug 23 and it was subsequently extended. The govt cut the conversion fee from 5% to 2% of guidance value for applications filed by that date. It has since returned to 5%. The campaign targeted 7 lakh eligible B-khata properties among 23 lakh in GBA limits. Eligible properties were those registered on or before Sept 30, 2024, with a clear tax history and no major encroachment. Despite the 60% fee rebate, only 80,400 applications had come in by the end of Aug. The first version of e-Aasthi was introduced in the erstwhile BBMP in Oct 2024. The new version is designed to link with Kaveri, Bescom and BWSSB, so that property and registration data is shared and records update automatically from e-khata details. title: Mumbai mangrove cover shrinks 17.41% in 18 years, study warns of threat to coastal biodiversity, concerns over fish breeding habitats
text: Mumbai's mangrove cover has decreased significantly, with a loss of approximately 30.20 square kilometers recorded (Representative image) MUMBAI: The city has lost nearly one-fifth of its mangrove cover in 18 years, raising concerns over the survival of natural fish nurseries that sustain coastal biodiversity and support fishing communities. Between 2006 and 2024, mangrove cover along the city's coastline declined by 17.41%, with researchers mapping 30.20 sq km of mangroves lost against just 11.32sqkm of new growth. The findings of a study published online on October 26 in Elsevier journal 'Total Environment Advances' highlight the growing ecological vulnerability of Mumbai's coastal landscape. The loss is significant not merely because the city is losing its green buffers, but because mangroves perform an important, less visible function: their intricate root systems provide shelter, food and nursery habitats for juvenile fish, prawns, crabs and other aquatic organisms. For Mumbai's fishing communities, the degradation of these habitats raises questions about the long-term health of nearby fishing waters. Mangrove ecosystems support the early stages of aquatic life, provide feeding grounds and contribute nutrients and organic matter to adjoining creeks and coastal waters. Their degradation can disrupt these ecological processes and potentially affect fish recruitment and the wider food chain. The study, Multi-temporal assessment of mangrove dynamics along the Mumbai coastline using satellite imagery and machine learning, by Vinod Kumar Yadav and Durgesh Kumar Jha, assessed four coastal sectors â Versova-Madh Island-Malad (VMM), Gorai Creek, Thane Creek and Sewri-Chembur-Trombay â using satellite images from 2006, 2012, 2018 and 2024. The researchers found that mapped mangrove area declined from 75.07sqkm in 2006 to 61.99sqkm in 2024. Their common-resolution transition analysis recorded 30.20sqkm of loss and 11.32sqkm of gain, resulting in a net reduction of 18.89sqkm. The largest net decline occurred between 2012 and 2018. The damage is not limited to the disappearance of mangrove patches. The composition of the surviving vegetation has also changed. Open mangrove cover declined by 76.80% and sparse mangrove cover by 19.28%, indicating substantial changes in the density and structure of the ecosystem. This matters because the ecological functions of a mangrove forest depend not just on its geographical spread but also on its health, density and continuity. For fisheries scientists, this raises an important question: how much of the loss and degradation of mangrove habitats is affecting the availability of breeding and nursery grounds for fish and shellfish in Mumbai's creeks? A decline in suitable juvenile habitats can potentially affect recruitment into adult fish populations, although the extent of any impact on fish stocks or fishing yields would need to be established through independent fisheries surveys. The study itself does not measure fish populations, species diversity or fishing catches. Its contribution is to establish the scale and geographical pattern of mangrove change, providing a scientific basis for further investigation into its consequences for aquatic biodiversity and fisheries. The researchers used four machine-learning methods â Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Trees and Support Vector Machine â to classify satellite imagery and map changes in mangrove cover. They also examined the effect of differences in satellite resolution. Between 2018 and 2024, the estimated decline was 5.03% at the native 10-metre resolution of Sentinel-2 imagery and 6.75% after aggregation to a common 30-metre resolution. Despite the difference in estimates, both analyses indicated a continuing decline. The implications extend to the city's protection against climate-related risks. Mangroves stabilise shorelines, trap sediments, help regulate nutrient cycles and reduce the force of waves and storm surges. Their degradation can leave coastal stretches more vulnerable to erosion and flooding, particularly as Mumbai faces increasingly intense rainfall and rising coastal risks. The findings also call for a closer examination of restoration efforts. A previous assessment cited in the paper found that 13 of 25 mangrove restoration sites assessed in Mumbai showed no growth between the start of restoration and 2022. This underlines why conservation cannot be measured merely by the number of saplings planted. Restoring tidal connectivity, suitable sediment conditions and the ecological processes that allow mangroves to regenerate is equally important. For Mumbai, the challenge is therefore twofold: prevent further destruction of existing mangrove forests and ensure that restoration produces functioning ecosystems capable of sustaining marine life. The latest satellite assessment provides a warning that the city's coastal green cover is under pressure, and that the consequences could reach far beyond its shoreline. Dr Nehru Prabakaran, Scientist, Wildlife Institute of India and an expert on mangroves ecosystem said, "Mangrove decline across the world has reduced in recent years due to several local and global initiatives. However, the mangroves closer to densely populated urban centres continue to experience degradation despite several management interventions." "This study on Mumbai Mangroves reflects similar trends. Addressing the factors influencing this mangrove decline is an urgent need, which will be critical for safeguarding the future of coastal ecosystems and their services," he added. title: Mitchell Santner scripts history, becomes first spinner with multiple four-wicket hauls against India
text: New Zealand's Mitchell Santner (AP) Mitchell Santner unleashed a spin masterclass against India in the second T20I in Christchurch on Saturday, dismantling the visitors' middle order with a sensational four-wicket haul. Although his effort ultimately went in vain as India pulled off a stunning four-wicket victory, the New Zealand captain etched his name into the record books against the three-time T20 World Cup champions. Watch Sitanshu Kotak Press Conference: Update on Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav in Playing XI and more Santner tears through India's middle order Defending New Zealand's total of 180/5, Santner turned the contest on its head after India's chase had begun to lose momentum. The left-arm spinner removed Abhishek Sharma for 27, with Nathan Smith taking a catch at deep midwicket, before producing a decisive spell that left the Indian batting line-up scrambling. Santner then bowled India captain Shreyas Iyer for seven, deceiving him with drift and flight as the batter attempted to slog across the line. He followed it up by dismissing Axar Patel for 11, with Daryl Mitchell completing an excellent relay catch near the boundary after Finn Allen intervened. The New Zealand skipper saved his best for Naman Dhir, who had briefly revived India's hopes with an aggressive 31 off 17 balls. Santner tempted Dhir with a flighted delivery outside off, and the batter's attempted inside-out loft ended in the hands of Glenn Phillips at extra cover. Dhir's dismissal in the 15th over left India reeling at 112/6, with the required rate climbing and New Zealand seemingly in control of the contest. Santner's figures of 4/21 reflected not just his ability to take wickets but also his knack for forcing batters into risky strokes under pressure. Unique record against India Santner returned figures of 4/21 in his four overs, becoming the first bowler to register multiple four-wicket hauls against India in men's T20Is. His latest effort came nearly a decade after his previous four-wicket haul against India, when he returned career-best figures of 4/11 in Nagpur during the 2016 T20 World Cup. title: âNo option but to bat at 5 or 6â: Tilak Varma on adapting to new role in Indiaâs T20I setup
text: Bengaluru: India's Tilak Varma (PTI Photo) India vice-captain Tilak Varma has acknowledged that moving away from his preferred No. 3 position to bat lower down the order presents a challenge, but the 23-year-old is confident that regular practice and mental preparation will help him adjust to the demands of his new role. Tilak has increasingly been used at No. 5 and 6 in T20Is as India continue to settle on their batting combination. While the Hyderabad batter admits that he finds it easier to bat higher up the order, he is focused on becoming a reliable finisher for the team. Watch Tilak Varma on batting at No. 5 and 6: âI want to finish games for the countryâ Speaking after the fifth and final T20I against the West Indies was washed out on Saturday night, Tilak said adapting to different batting positions requires considerable work, particularly when the responsibility is to close out games. "It's not that easy to change the numbers from 3 to 5 and 6. It will be slightly challenging. But I have been working on that. How can I finish the games? I have said that I love finishing the games for the country," he said. "So, for me as an individual, if you see, it will be easier batting at 3. But unfortunately, now I should bat at 5 or 6 because we have got that combination at the top right now." The left-hander's record at No. 6 offers encouragement. Across nine matches in that position, he averages 65.66 at a strike rate of 195. In 26 combined innings at Nos. 5 and 6, he has scored at an average of 46 and a strike rate of 158. However, the arrival of Ishan Kishan, captain Shreyas Iyer 's presence at No. 4 and the management's decision to continue with the Abhishek Sharma-Sanju Samson opening combination have left Tilak with a reduced role in the middle order. Kishan has been batting at No. 3 and has impressed in the position, leaving Tilak with little choice but to embrace the finishing responsibilities. "Kishan is batting at number 3 now, and he is batting really brilliantly there. So, for me now, I think there is no option but to bat at 5 and 6 and do the job for the team. "So, I am mentally prepared for that role. And if you see the last few games, I have won from there. So, I am pretty confident to do well there as well," he added. Tilak working on his finishing skills Tilak said he has been putting in extra work in the nets to expand his shot-making range and improve his ability to score quickly when batting with limited time at the crease. He explained that players operating at Nos. 5 and 6 often have only five or six overs to make an impact, making it important to capitalise on scoring opportunities, including when bowlers deliver slower balls within their hitting range. "Yeah, we should do that, otherwise, it will be slightly tough. When you go in to bat as a finisher, if a slower one comes into your arc, you should go for 6. Otherwise, if you see in T20, most of the time, if you go into that role of 5 or 6, you will get a maximum of 5 to 6 overs to bat. "So, I have changed personally. I have been in this role in my childhood as well. I have got the shots going all over the ground. So, I am confident that if I bat at 3 or 5, I have got the technique to adapt. So, if I practise for 1 or 2 days, I can do any role for the team. "Now, if I come back to No. 3, I can adapt after a day or two of practice. I am confident of batting anywhere," he noted. Busy schedule no excuse, says India vice-captain India's players have endured a packed run of fixtures over the past few months, travelling across the United Kingdom, Japan and India. The team will soon head to New Zealand for an all-format tour. Tilak admitted that the demands of consecutive series, different time zones and changing conditions can be difficult, particularly for younger players. However, he stressed that handling such challenges is part of playing international cricket. "It will be slightly challenging. But as professional cricketers, we can't give any excuse because when we play back-to-back series, there will be different time zones and all those things. We are used to it now. If you see, for any youngster coming into the team, it will be slightly challenging. "But again, you are playing for the country and at the highest level. So, as I said, you should be mentally strong enough to prepare for any challenge, any conditions so that you can become a bigger player," he added. Tilak highlights positives from West Indies series Despite the challenges, Tilak believes India have several encouraging takeaways from the West Indies series that they can carry into the upcoming assignments in New Zealand. He pointed to the team's consistent run-scoring, with India crossing the 200-run mark in every match, as a major positive. He also acknowledged the contributions of Nitish Reddy, Shivam Dube and Naman Dhir. "There have been quite a few good things. Especially in the batting, every game we have scored over 200 plus. So, that's a big positive, and that too, we haven't got a proper all-rounder in the team. We have played both Nitish (Reddy) and (Shivam) Dubey as well. title: Persons with disabilities seek clarity on adapted vehicles under Delhiâs entry restrictions
text: New Delhi: With Delhiâs ban on the entry of non-Delhi-registered vehicles below the BS-VI emission standard now in force, confusion prevails among the public and police personnel over whether the adapted vehicles used by persons with disabilities are exempted or not. Persons with disabilities have pointed to a Nov 28, 2024 order of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), which allowed adapted BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel vehicles used by persons with disabilities to operate even during higher stages of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). âConsidering practical difficulties being faced or likely to be faced by the persons with disabilities in their daily commuting, the request for exemption for use of adapted BS-III Petrol and BS-IV Diesel vehicles even during restriction period under Stage-III of GRAP has been examined in the Commission and considered for permitting plying of such BS-III Petrol/BS-IV Diesel vehicles even under GRAP Stage III & above only as a matter of exception. Enforcement agencies in Delhi-NCR may be, accordingly, advised to permit plying of all such adapted vehicles for personal use of persons with disabilities,â the order stated. However, persons with disabilities claim they are being stopped at Delhiâs borders amid uncertainty over whether the exemption applies under the new winter pollution restrictions. Satendra Singh, a disability rights activist and a doctor at GTB Hospital, said he was stopped by a police officer while travelling from his home in Vasundhara, Ghaziabad, to the hospital. âI showed him the CAQM order. However, he said it is of 2024. Though he permitted me to go today, he said I wonât be allowed from Tuesday,â said Singh. Singh said he has written to CAQM and Delhi govtâs environment department seeking clarity and exemption for adapted vehicles registered outside Delhi. title: In 2024, a Maharashtra couple lost their jobs and set off on one motorcycle with limited savings; over 80 days they rode 16,428 km across 22 states and four Union Territories, later earning record recognition
text: A sudden job loss in 2024 became the starting point of an unexpected adventure for Samrat and Varshali Dambe. With their corporate careers interrupted, the Maharashtra couple decided to use the uncertain months ahead to fulfil a dream they had shared for years: riding around Indiaâs borders. Starting from their village of Mhapral in Ratnagiri district, they set off on their motorcycle with limited savings and no guarantee that they could complete the route. Their expedition, called the Art India Ride, took them across 16,428 km in 80 days, through challenging roads, changing weather and remote regions. Along the way, they discovered the kindness of strangers and experienced the country beyond familiar maps. The journey eventually earned them recognition from the India Book of Records, but its real value lay in the experiences they gathered on the road. A childhood sketch became a shared road trip Samratâs idea of riding around India began when he was 12. He would draw the countryâs outline and imagine following its borders on a motorcycle. Years later, the dream became something he and Varshali wanted to experience together. The couple had been riding together since 2018 and bought a Benelli TRK in 2022, hoping to take on longer journeys. Before their expedition, Samrat worked in digital marketing at a multinational company, while Varshali was a digital marketing manager at an agency. Their plans changed when both lost their jobs around June 2024. They suddenly had three to four months without the routine of work, but their finances were uncertain. âWe didnât know if we had enough money to complete the journey. We did not even know what we would do when we came back. But we knew that if we kept waiting for the right time, we might never go,â they recalled. They initially considered covering only half the country, as their savings were limited. However, by August, they had decided to begin. Heavy rain in South India also led them to change their original route just eight days before departure. They chose to start with Gujarat and travel clockwise. The couple began the Art India Ride in September 2024 and returned to Mhapral on December 8. Five bags, one motorcycle and a strict spending limit The journey required more than enthusiasm. Their motorcycle averaged around 20 km per litre, making fuel a major expense. They set a daily budget of Rs 3,500 for fuel, food and accommodation, usually choosing rooms that cost between Rs 1,000 and Rs 1,500. They also made a practical agreement: if their savings dropped to Rs 40,000, they would return home and look for jobs. Their belongings for 80 days fitted into five bags. They carried a few clothes, riding gear, raincoats, winter layers, laptops, cameras, documents and a basic toolkit. Rather than planning every stop in advance, they generally decided where to go next a day or two before setting off. The route took them through western, northern, northeastern and southern India, including Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The road did not always make things easy. Near the Gujarat-Rajasthan border, a storm and a long, isolated stretch left them anxious. In Ladakh, they faced freezing temperatures, poor network connectivity and hotels that had shut for the season. Around Pangong Lake, the temperature fell to minus 12 degrees Celsius. At Upshi, Varshali was shivering in the cold. They eventually found a local Maharashtrian who helped them arrange a room with a heater. The experience reminded them that preparation mattered, but so did knowing when to seek help. Strangers turned unfamiliar places into home Some of the coupleâs strongest memories came from people they met along the way. In Punjab, a family welcomed them into their home. In Tawang, a woman from Maharashtra offered them blessings and greeted them with a traditional Tibetan white shawl. In Bhalukpong, Arunachal Pradesh, an elderly couple running a cafe treated Samrat with the affection of a son. When the travellers returned to meet them on their way back, the uncle became emotional as they prepared to leave. Another memorable meeting happened at a breakfast stall in North Bengal. A group of people noticed the Maharashtra registration on their motorcycle and began asking about their journey. One of them, Kolkata-based corporate professional Arun Sircar, told the couple that travelling across India had once been his own dream. He and his wife later invited Samrat and Varshali home, arranged a meal and gave them a place to stay. For the couple, the meeting showed how their journey could connect with people who had never travelled the same roads. âAfter travelling 16,428 kilometres, it felt like one giant, compassionate family,â Samrat said, describing the warmth they received across different regions. From a record to a riding community The couple spent around Rs 3.75 lakh on the expedition, including fuel, food, accommodation and motorcycle maintenance. They had not set out to earn a record, but a friend encouraged them to submit their journey for recognition. They provided photographs, fuel receipts and other documents. In January 2025, the India Book of Records recognised both Samrat and Varshali as IBR Achievers for their 80-day, 16,428-km expedition. Its individual entries record the ride as covering 20 states and three Union Territories on their Benelli TRK 502X motorcycle. The experience also inspired their next step. On April 6, 2025, they started Souls of Motorcycle, a riding community intended to help enthusiasts learn, travel responsibly and build confidence on the road. According to the couple, the group has grown to more than 700 members, with over 8,000 Instagram followers. For Samrat, riding also offers a way to stay focused on the present. The sound of the engine and the attention required on the road, he says, make the experience feel like meditation. Their journey began after an unexpected career setback, with no guarantee that their savings would last. They returned with a record, new friendships and a different understanding of the country. More than the distance, the Art India Ride showed them what could happen when two people chose to begin before every uncertainty had been resolved. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: 180 runs, 1 wicket, 4 T20Is! 'Playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar was a mistake': Ex-India star questions selectors
text: Bhuvneshwar Kumar (BCCI Photo) NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has questioned the selectors' decision to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back into the T20I team, calling his inclusion in the recent series against New Zealand a mistake. Bhuvneshwar returned to India's T20I side after a gap of four years but struggled to make an impact. He managed just one wicket while conceding 180 runs in four matches. Watch Tim Seifert on New Zealand's comeback, India's bowling & Glenn Phillips' record breaking series India, led by Shreyas Iyer, started the five-match series with three consecutive wins but lost the final two games. Following the series, Pathan questioned the purpose of bringing back the experienced pacer when the next T20 World Cup is still some distance away. "In my opinion, where did the selectors go wrong? They made a mistake by playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar in this series. Look, there is no doubt that Bhuvneshwar is a good bowler and a senior player. However, playing him here, when the T20 World Cup is nowhere near, was questionable. If you were preparing Bhuvneshwar for the 50-over World Cup, which is closer, that would have made sense," Irfan said in a video on his YouTube channel. Bhuvneshwar struggles in New Zealand series Bhuvneshwar's comeback in the first T20I did not go as planned. Playing his first T20I in four years, he went wicketless and conceded 49 runs in four overs at an economy rate of 12.25. He picked up his only wicket of the series in the second T20I, dismissing Daryl Mitchell for six. However, he conceded 50 runs in his four overs. The experienced pacer went wicketless again in the third match, giving away 40 runs. He missed the fourth T20I before returning for the series finale. Bhuvneshwar was unable to make an impact in the final match as well. He conceded 41 runs in four overs without taking a wicket. Pathan says young pacers missed an opportunity Pathan believes Bhuvneshwar's selection also meant that young fast bowlers missed out on valuable international experience. "By including him in this series, however, you missed out on giving young fast bowlers an opportunity. A youngster could have played in his place and gained valuable experience. Mayank [Yadav] could have played all the matches and gained that exposure, while Prince Yadav could have played too. You missed a valuable opportunity for your fast bowlers to gain good experience on New Zealand soil," he added. Pathan also made it clear that his comments were not based only on Bhuvneshwar's performances in the series. He acknowledged that the senior pacer was also unlucky at times. title: In 2003, Alicia Keys co-founded a charity to help children affected by HIV; two decades later, it has raised $86.6 million and supports 9.3 million children, young people and families in 28 countries
text: Alicia Keys, 45, is now a mother of five (two biological children and three stepchildren). Motherhood came to her as an adult, but the instinct to look after children was there well before that. Long before she had children of her own, she was already caring about children on the brink of neglect. Alicia Keys was just 20 when she travelled to South Africa as part of MTVâs Staying Alive campaign. During the visit, she went to clinics where pregnant women and new mothers were confronting the reality of HIV/AIDS, including the risk of passing the virus on to their babies. She also witnessed widows and children orphaned by AIDS struggling to survive. âI couldnât turn my back on all Iâd seen,â Keys told WebMD at the time. The experience inspired her to co-found Keep a Child Alive in 2003 alongside AIDS activist Leigh Blake, with the aim of helping children and families affected by HIV/AIDS access life-saving medication and essential support. Twenty years later, the non-profit charity had raised $86.6 million, worked in 28 countries and supported over 9.3 million children, young people and families. A trip that changed many lives At 20, Keys travelled to South Africa as part of MTVâs Staying Alive campaign, which focused on HIV and AIDS. What she saw there changed her life and many others for the better. âAt the time, a lot of women didnât realize that if you are positive and you breastfeed your baby, your baby will contract it,â Keys told People in 2019. âThe moms just wanted medicine to keep them alive. That was the first time as a 20-year-old that I was aware of the injustice. I thought, âHow can something be available, but you canât have it because youâre poor?â I just felt like that was a death sentence. Thatâs what outraged me and motivated me. When I came back, I was never the same.â She couldnât just turn her back on these children and women. She had to do something. Keep a Child Alive That something became a non-profit organisation called Keep a Child Alive. True to its name, its mission was to keep children alive. The aim was to support children facing the most challenging circumstances. Keys built the organisation with AIDS activist Leigh Blake, who had already worked on the issue for years. Blake had helped organise a 2001 remake of Marvin Gayeâs âWhatâs Going Onâ to raise AIDS awareness, with Bono as co-executive producer, and had funded a clinic in Kenya. Keep a Child Alive launched in 2003 with a simple aim: to get life-saving AIDS medication to children and families who could not afford it. Blake took the lead on the medical and fundraising side, while Keys became the public face. Keysâ contribution over the years has been steady. Its annual fundraiser, the Black Ball, has been a regular fixture on New Yorkâs calendar. The non-profit has 41 partners, according to the organisation. The Hellâs Kitchen partnership was one of the groupâs more visible recent efforts. Starting in April 2024, the production and ticketing partner TodayTix Group pledged $1 from every ticket sold for the Broadway run. In October, the show announced that it had donated $1 million, including matching gifts. The charity said that sum would reach 18,250 children across eight countries. A later statement put the total at more than $1.5 million. âI have taken such pride in being a co-founder of Keep a Child Alive since its creation over 20 years ago and all the lives we have been able to touch and all that we have been able to accomplish so far. Hell's Kitchen is about a 17-year-old girl trying to find her way in NYC. Both Hell's Kitchen and Keep a Child Alive believe that every child in the world should have the opportunity to thrive. I feel immense gratitude that we can partner, with equal passion, to create an even greater force for change,â Alicia Keys said in a statement released on the non-profitâs website. Keys started the organisation to get antiretroviral drugs to children who had no other route to treatment. It was an emergency effort to reach families in South Africa, Uganda, India, Kenya and Rwanda. Over time, the mission widened to cover health, education and human rights, though HIV remains at its centre. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: 'WTC win was no fluke': Temba Bavuma slams 'critics' after statement win over Australia
text: South Africa's captain Temba Bavuma celebrates after hitting a century on day three of the second cricket test match between South Africa and Australia, in Gqeberha, South Africa. AP/PTI South Africa captain Temba Bavuma believes his team have answered questions about their World Test Championship (WTC) triumph after completing a 2-1 series win over Australia. The Proteas came back from a defeat in the opening Test to win the next two matches, including the series decider by 176 runs at Newlands on Saturday. South Africa's recent run includes qualifying for the 2025 WTC final even after forfeiting a series in New Zealand, beating defending champions Australia in the final at Lord's, drawing a series in Pakistan and winning a Test series in India for the first time in 25 years. title: After paying Rs 1.2 lakh for a five-star hotel membership, woman couldn't get promised luxury stays; consumer commission awards Rs 1.3 lakh with interest
text: AI generated image used for representative purpose NEW DELHI: A Punjab district consumer commission has directed a travel agency to refund Rs 1.2 lakh to a woman who alleged that the company failed to provide the promised luxury hotel accommodation under its prepaid holiday membership. The bench also asked the company to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for harassment and litigation expenses. Why did the agency denied Radisson hotel According to the commission order, Niti Bansal, a resident of Dhuri in Sangrur district, purchased a five-year membership from Club Infication on September 1, 2024, after being told that she would receive six nights and seven days of accommodation in five-star hotels every year. The membership was offered for a period of five years and the complainant paid a total of Rs 1,20,000 through online transactions on September 1, 2 and 4, 2024. The company allegedly told her that hotel stays could be booked by informing its representatives at least 48 working hours in advance. The scheme also had a blackout period from December 20 to January 10. On September 5, 2024, Bansal approached the company's representatives to book a hotel room in Chandigarh. After being told that the company needed 48 hours to make the booking, she changed her proposed stay to September 15-17, 2024. The company then sent her a list of available hotels. However, according to her complaint, none of the options was a five-star hotel. She wanted a room at the Radisson or a hotel of equivalent status. The complainant checked the Radisson's availability online and found that rooms appeared to be available. However, the company's representatives told her that only the hotels shared with her on WhatsApp could be booked. She alleged that the company refused to arrange accommodation at a hotel from the list provided to her when she purchased the membership. The complainant later sent a legal notice to the company on December 26, 2024, seeking a resolution. In its reply, Club Infication claimed that the package covered three-star and five-star hotels depending on availability on its portal. It further added that the Radisson and Ramada were not available through the portal. The complainant approached the commission, alleging deficiency in service. She sought a refund of Rs 1.2 lakh with 18 percent annual interest from September 1, 2024, Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental tension and harassment, and Rs 55,000 towards litigation expenses. Commission's finding The bench of president Jot Naranjan Singh Gill and members Sarita Garg and Kanwaljeet Singh examined the membership documents, hotel list, WhatsApp conversations and other records submitted by the complainant. The commission noted that the membership terms covered six nights and seven days of accommodation at premium locations in India and abroad. It also considered the company's reply to the legal notice, in which it said hotel availability depended on the options listed on its portal. âEx.C-5 copy of the reply of the legal notice and Ex.C-10 copy of whatsapp chat proves that the opposite party no.1 failed to accommodate the complainant any hotels as per the terms and conditions of the Luxury Holiday Pre Paid Package,â the bench said. It found that the company had failed to provide accommodation in hotels according to the package terms. âWe are of the view that offering a hotel in place of luxury accommodation amounts to substantial deviation from the service for which the complainant paid consideration,â it further added. The commission also noted that the company had not appeared to contest the complaint despite notice. It proceeded ex parte against the opposite parties on December 5, 2025, and considered the complainant's evidence, which remained unrebutted. âIn view of the facts and circumstances it is established that opposite party no.1 has failed to provide the service in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Luxury Holiday Pre Paid Package purchased by the complainant. The same constitutes deficiency in service on the part of the opposite party no.1,â the commission concluded. Final order The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Sangrur, allowed the complaint and directed Club Infication to: Refund Rs 1,20,000 to the complainant. Pay 7 percent annual interest on the refund from March 5, 2025, the date the complaint was filed, until realisation. Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental pain, agony and harassment. Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses. The company was directed to comply within 60 days of receiving a copy of the order. The commission passed the order on October 12, 2026. The fixed payout ordered, excluding interest, is Rs 1.3 lakh. The commission awarded interest at 7 percent per annum, rather than the 18 percent sought by the complainant, and ordered Rs 10,000 in compensation and litigation expenses, against the combined Rs 1.05 lakh she had claimed under those heads.
